WHAT WAS LEARNED.

1. A FREEZE READING CAN BE STRICTER THAN THE CONTRACT, AND THAT COSTS ITERATIONS
   TOO.  Iteration 16 filed candidate 63 as needing an authorization the PRD had
   already granted twice over - once naming the values, once ruling the parameter
   free.  The loop has repeatedly paid for reading a stale predecessor's summary
   instead of the contract; this is the same failure with the sign flipped, and
   the same fix applies: re-read prd.md, not the last iteration's note about it.

2. THE DEFECT'S SHAPE IS THE FAMILIAR ONE, ONE LAYER OUT.  "Known on one side of
   a seam and never carried across" is the class that produced candidates 53, 60
   and the four Phase H/J blockers.  Here the two sides were a measurement
   (93.4 % at 0.35/0.1) and a deployment (0.5/0.2), and nothing in the repo made
   them the same number.  The fix is the same shape as J4's: name the thing once,
   and make the path that ships it carry the name.

3. WHAT A HASH CHANGE MEANS DEPENDS ON WHICH CHANGE IT IS.  Every redeploy in
   this loop's history has checked `provider_manifest_hash 61d97ffe…` UNCHANGED as
   evidence of a clean deployment.  After the recalibration that check inverts:
   an unchanged identity hash proves the recalibration did NOT happen.  Recorded
   in LOCAL_DEPLOYMENT.md, in the Validation fence's finalize recipe and in the
   N-recal block so a future redeploy does not read the intended change as drift.

BLOCKERS: none for this iteration.

WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT DONE.  The host manifest was NOT regenerated and no host
was touched: the deployed service still carries 0.5 / 0.2 and would still run the
album at 75.0 %.  Regenerating it is a step of Phase N's redeploy (gate -> merge
-> push -> redeploy), which the certification-order rule puts after the merge and
which this iteration is not authorized to run on its own.  The recipe, with the
--dry-run first and the hash-change warning, is in the Validation fence.

the next step and the only Phase N item needing neither an operator nor a host.

  docs/adr/0003-live-session-audio-retention.md   NEW - the decision
  scripts/ralph-afk/context.md                    N-tape block, stands-where, Ground

WHY AN ADR AND NOT A CONTEXT.MD PARAGRAPH.  The decision changes how a PRD
ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE is read, so it has to be reviewable by the operator in the
place they already keep design decisions - they wrote ADR-0002 and
docs/design-streaming-diarization.md themselves, and §8 of that design lists
"Retention TTL / privacy posture for stored session audio" as an OPEN QUESTION.
This answers that question in its own file.  Same precedent as iteration 17
touching LOCAL_DEPLOYMENT.md: a tracked doc supporting an authorized phase.

THE FRAMING THAT MADE IT DECIDABLE, AND IT IS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED.  The clause
is NOT a prohibition on audio reaching a disk.  Live audio touches disk on EVERY
SPAN TODAY:
    live_adapters.py:298        TemporaryDirectory(prefix="mtd-live-", dir=scratch)
                                -> the decoder's wav, removed on context exit
    live_provider_bundle.py:561 TemporaryDirectory() -> the identity encoder's
In memory the horizon is longer and also bounded: LiveSession prunes committed
frames against max_retained_samples 960000 (60 s), a domain-contract value.
So the clause is a statement about a HORIZON - today one span, ~2.5 s - and the
loop's own recorded hygiene evidence (`live-runs/` 0 entries, no surviving
/tmp/mtd-live-*) is exactly that horizon holding in F1, F2 and F3.  The question
is therefore how far the horizon may move, and the answer is ONE MEETING.  A
blanket enforcement forbids step 2 and with it ADR-0002's own acceptance bar
(convergence needs a sweep and a sweep needs a substrate); a blanket waiver hands
an unbounded write path to a host that also serves the batch service, whose
"unharmed" clause is in the same PRD bar.  Neither reading was available.

THE SEVEN RULES (full text and reasoning in the ADR).
  D1  The horizon becomes the session; "persisted" keeps its force against
      anything longer-lived.
  D2  Retention is OPT-IN and OFF BY DEFAULT.  Two reasons: every gate this loop
      recorded was measured against a no-tape service, and a privacy posture must
      never arrive as a side effect of upgrading a binary.
  D3  DEFAULT TTL AFTER SESSION END IS ZERO.  ADR-0002 runs its final sweep at
      session end and the album is the compressed context handed forward, so
      nothing in the design needs the audio afterwards.  At the default the PRD
      clause still holds LITERALLY at every boundary an operator can observe
      after a meeting.  A positive TTL is STATED BY THE DEPLOYMENT, never
      defaulted by a tool - candidate 63's rule, applied a second time.
  D4  ONE DECLARED ROOT: 0600 in 0700, outside the checkout (a rollback is
      `git checkout <sha>` and `git clean` must never be a reaper), NOT on the
      batch runs filesystem, and on a filesystem that enforces modes.  /mnt/d is
      disqualified TWICE (9p drvfs without `metadata` -> 777 and chmod is a
      no-op; and it is where BATCH_RUNS_DIR and MOSS_RUNS_DIR both live).  ext4
      ~/.local/share/moss-transcribe-diarize/live/ satisfies all four today.
  D5  The cap is declared and STORAGE PRESSURE DEGRADES THE TAPE, NEVER THE
      MEETING - the third amendment's governing rule applied to a disk: typed
      degradation with the byte counts, sweeps lose their substrate, the session
      continues, frame acks never block.
  D6  THE SERVICE REAPS, AT STARTUP TOO.  A TTL that only fires while the process
      lives is not a retention policy; helper-lease expiry already makes an
      abandoned meeting terminal, so no new timer is needed for that half.
  D7  Still absolutely forbidden: audio on the Mac beyond the outbox's in-memory
      frames, in a log/journal/telemetry/snapshot/event/portal response, in any
      evidence directory pulled off a host, or under batch runs/.  The token half
      of the clause is untouched and keeps its absolute reading.

THE ONE MEASURED ARGUMENT THAT IS EASY TO MISS.  A runaway tape breaks the PRD's
"batch service unharmed" clause WITHOUT TOUCHING THE BATCH SERVICE.  server.py:447
`_admit_upload_request` answers 507 Insufficient storage whenever
`disk_usage(runs_dir).free < 2 * content_length + 512 MB`, and at ADR-0002's
~0.3 GB/hr that headroom is under two hours of ONE meeting.  That is why D4(3) is
a rule and not a preference, and it is the kind of coupling that would otherwise
have been found by a red certification run three phases later.

WHAT THE CLAUSE BECOMES, SO IT STAYS TESTABLE RATHER THAN BECOMING A WAIVER.  Two
forms, selected by whether a root is declared:
  * undeclared (today's deployed server): UNCHANGED - live-runs/ 0 entries, no
    surviving /tmp/mtd-live-*, no audio artifact on either host.  Every recorded
    certification run therefore keeps its meaning.
  * declared: audio ONLY under that root; every tape maps to a session active or
    within TTL; modes 0600/0700; total bytes <= the declared cap; nothing under
    the checkout, nothing under batch runs/, nothing on the Mac.

VALIDATION.  Doc-only change; the evidence that matters is that every source
claim the decision rests on is true at this tip, each checked by one command:

      -> /mnt/d/Coding/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize/live-runs - i.e. BOTH runs trees
         are on the drvfs mount, which is D4(3)+D4(4) in one line     CONFIRMED
  grep -n max_retained_samples live_session.py -> the 60 s in-memory bound
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
      -> 662 passed, 2 skipped, 368 subtests (unchanged from iteration 17, as a
         doc-only change must be)
  git status --porcelain -> only the two files above

WHAT WAS LEARNED.

1. A CLAUSE THAT LOOKS ABSOLUTE CAN BE A HORIZON, AND READING IT LITERALLY WOULD
   HAVE BEEN WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.  "No raw audio is persisted" was already
   false as a literal statement about the running service - the decoder writes a
   wav per span - and the loop has been certifying it green for six phases by
   measuring the horizon (nothing survives) rather than the letter (nothing is
   written).  Naming that explicitly is what made the ADR-0002 collision
   tractable in one iteration instead of an authorization request.

2. THE FAMILIAR CLASS SHOWS UP IN STORAGE TOO.  "A condition the design
   contemplates is handled everywhere except the path that ends the meeting" is
   this loop's signature defect (H/J's four blockers, 53, 56).  A full disk during
   a taped meeting is the same shape waiting to be written, which is why D5 rules
   it a degradation BEFORE the code exists rather than after a red soak.

3. A DECISION RECORD IS CHEAPER THAN THE CODE IT CONSTRAINS, AND ONLY IF IT COMES
   FIRST.  D2 (opt-in) is the rule that preserves every gate this loop has already
   recorded; had step 2 shipped default-on, F1/F2/F3's hygiene evidence would all
   have needed re-running against a service that behaves differently.

BLOCKERS: none for this iteration.

manifest, unit or env file gained a retention key.  The ADR deliberately does not
decide the on-disk format or gap-manifest schema (ADR-0002 §Decision 1 and design
§3.2 already fix raw PCM + JSON index, WAV on demand, teed at the mixer's sealed-
interval commit), whether the album may outlive a meeting (derived data, not raw
audio - but cross-meeting albums are ADR-0002 §8 fog and stay closed), the numeric
TTL/cap for any deployment, or re-ASR of the tape (forbidden by ADR-0002).

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP.  Phase N step 2 itself - the tape recorder, in

The alternative - gating and merging steps 1+63 alone - stays contraindicated by
the amendment's own words: the album alone is "a terminal-state failure if shipped
alone", and a merge is the loop's scarcest resource.

      -> 32 passed in 3.59 s
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider
      -> 694 passed, 2 skipped, 368 subtests in 70.73 s
         (662 -> 694 = exactly the 32 new nodes; the two skips are still the

  git status --porcelain -> exactly the two new files, nothing else

RED-BEFORE, BY THREE SEMANTIC REVERTS - 15 OF THE 32 NODES.  The module is new,
so "red before" cannot mean a prior commit; it means the suite fails when the
behaviour it claims is removed.  Each revert was applied to the module, run, and
restored from a byte-identical copy (sha re-verified after each restore).
  1. `_Track.offset_samples` -> `return self.sample_count`, i.e. place frames in
     ARRIVAL ORDER like a naive appender               -> 8 RED
     (duplicates, reorder, the dropped-frame gap, burst loss, the late fill,
      resume's gap manifest, silence-vs-drop, the skipped mixer interval)
  2. the cap check and the TTL comparison -> `if False:` -> 3 RED
     (cap degradation, positive-TTL retention, the crashed-tape startup reap)
  3. D4's four admission rules -> `if False:`            -> 4 RED
     (root inside the checkout, root sharing a filesystem with a runs tree, root
      inside a runs tree by name, a filesystem that does not enforce modes)

THE SHAPE THAT LANDED.  Three tracks per session - system.pcm, microphone.pcm,
mixed.pcm, raw PCM16 mono at the canonical 16 kHz - plus index.json, which is the
gap manifest and the resume checkpoint.  Every placement is computed from the
frame's capture_timestamp_ns, never from arrival order.  Coverage is a merged
half-open interval list and THE GAP MANIFEST IS ITS COMPLEMENT, so a late frame
removes a gap instead of appending a correction, and a resumed tape reconstructs
coverage from the persisted gaps + sample_count (one representation, so the two
can never disagree).  index.json is republished atomically - staged file plus
os.replace, the lesson the port-publish race already cost this repo a merge -
on EVERY append, which is what makes checkpoint/resume exact at any frame rather
than at a checkpoint interval.

FOUR DECISIONS, RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT RE-ARGUED.

1. THE TAPE NEVER RAISES BECAUSE OF A FRAME.  Cap reached, write failed, or a
   frame it cannot place (wrong sample rate, bad PCM length, tape already ended)
   -> one typed degradation carrying the byte counts (tape_capacity_exhausted /
   tape_write_failed / tape_frame_not_admissible), taping stops, the call returns
   and the meeting continues on live labels alone.  ADR-0003 D5, which is the
   third amendment's governing rule applied to a disk.  This is the loop's
   signature defect class - a non-fatal condition wearing a fatal type - ruled
   out BEFORE the code has a caller rather than after a red soak.

2. `declared()` REFUSES A ROOT LOUDLY, AT CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT ONE IS AN
   EXCEPTION.  A root that cannot hold audio safely must stop the service
   starting with retention enabled, not silently disable it - the opposite
   default from (1), and deliberately so: (1) is about a frame during a meeting,
   this is about a deployment before one.  The checkout boundary is derived from
   Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2], never named, so the rule holds on any
   host; D4(4) is asserted by chmod-then-read-back, which is the only way to
   catch a 9p drvfs mount where chmod is a silent no-op; and D4(3) is checked
   BOTH by st_dev equality and by name containment, because on a single-filesystem
   host the device test alone cannot see "inside the runs tree".

3. THE REAPER NEVER DELETES WHAT IT CANNOT READ AS A TAPE.  An unreadable, torn
   or foreign directory under the root is logged and skipped.  A reaper that
   removes what it does not understand is a worse failure than a tape that
   outlives its TTL.  A crashed meeting's tape has no `ended_at`, so it is aged
   from `updated_at` - which is precisely what lets D6's startup reap reach it;
   an unfinished tape treated as "not yet ended" would be immortal, which is the
   failure D6 exists to name.

4. THE TTL SUBTRACTS TWO time.time() READINGS, DELIBERATELY, AND SAYS SO.  A
   retention deadline has to survive a process restart and time.monotonic() does
   not.  This is P4's recorded exception (persisted/expiry timestamps), but the
   shipped "Duration vs timestamp" contract reads as a blanket prohibition, so
   the module states the exemption at the site.  The direction is also checked:
   on the one host where the clock is KNOWN to step, it steps BACKWARDS, and a
   backward step can only delay a reap, never make one premature.

WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT DONE - AND THIS IS THE PART A LATER READER MUST NOT MISS.
NOTHING CALLS THIS MODULE.  No line of live_transport.py, live_mixer.py or
live_ingest.py changed; no manifest, env or unit key exists; no deployment
declares a root.  The deployed service is byte-for-byte unchanged and every
recorded hygiene result (live-runs/ 0 entries, no surviving /tmp/mtd-live-*)
keeps its meaning.  That is ADR-0003 D2 working as designed, not an omission -
but it does mean STEP 2 IS NOT FINISHED, and a green 694 must not be read as a
shipped tape.  Gate C's "byte-exact under real outbox replay" is proved against
the appender, not against the wired path.

WHAT WAS LEARNED.

1. THE INGRESS ALREADY NORMALISES WHAT GATE C TESTS, AND THE APPENDER STILL HAS
   TO SURVIVE IT.  LiveLaneIngress refuses a frame that is not the lane's next
   sequence, so downstream of it reorder is impossible and the rebase path can
   never fire in production.  Gate C nevertheless replays raw outbox retry order
   INTO THE APPENDER, so the appender's contract is wider than its wiring.  Two
   of the 32 nodes exist only for that gap, and the rebase they exercise is the
   most expensive code in the module - worth keeping precisely because the day
   the tee point moves upstream of the ingress, it is the only thing standing
   between a reordered replay and a tape whose every offset is wrong.

2. A GAP MANIFEST DERIVED FROM COVERAGE CANNOT DRIFT FROM THE FILE; ONE WRITTEN
   ALONGSIDE IT CAN.  The first design held gaps as their own list and appended
   an entry when a sequence was skipped.  It needed a second rule for the late
   frame that fills one, and a third for the resume that has to reconcile them.
   Complement-of-coverage needs none: the late-fill node and the resume node are
   the same code path, and there is no state in which the manifest and the tape
   disagree.

3. "CAPTURED SILENCE" AND "DROPPED FRAME" ARE THE SAME BYTES AND MUST NOT BE THE
   SAME FACT.  Both are zeros on disk.  Only the manifest tells a quiet room from
   a lost frame, and a sweep seeded from the wrong one would relabel exactly the
   seconds that never arrived.  There is a node asserting both regions are zero
   AND that only one is a gap.

BLOCKERS: none for this iteration.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP.  Wire it, in one iteration, inside
moss_transcribe_diarize/ + tests/: `append_lane_frame` after the v2 ingress ack
in live_transport.py's frame route, `append_mixed` at
LiveCompatibilityMixer.admit_available's sealed commit (the tee point ADR-0002
names), `release()` on the stop/terminal paths that already call
v2_mixers.release, and `reap()` once at service start.  The store is constructed
only when a root is declared, so the wiring's own red-before is that the deployed
configuration (no root) must produce a byte-identical service - assert that, not
just the taped path.  The declaration surface itself (an ops/moss-live.env key
plus its finalizer/manifest treatment) is a second, separable change and should
NOT be bundled: candidate 63 already established that a free deployed parameter
is stated by the deployment, and the TTL and cap are two more of them.

================================================================================

TARGET.  Iteration 19's recommended next step, and the only Phase N item needing
neither an operator nor a host: wire `live_tape.py` to the transport.  Step 2's

of a seam, uncalled from the other" shape as candidate 60 - a green 694 was not
a shipped tape.

VALIDATION.  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
  -> 703 passed / 2 skipped / 368 subtests in 70.59 s   (was 694/2/368)
Focused: tests/test_live_api.py 33, tests/test_live_tape.py 37,
tests/test_live_helper_failure.py 12 -> 82 collected, all green in 4.5 s.

PAYLOAD - 6 files, +528/-4.  moss_transcribe_diarize/app/live_tape.py (+117,
LiveSessionTapeRecorder), live_transport.py (+57), live_helper_failure.py (+7),

THE RED-BEFORE IS FOUR SEMANTIC REVERTS, EACH NAMING A DIFFERENT NODE.  Sources
copied to /tmp/i20-redbefore first and restored after each; the suite was green

  revert                                                  red nodes
  ------------------------------------------------------  ---------
  1. drop `tapes.append_lane_frame` + `_tape_mixed` in     1
     the frames route                                       (the taped route)
  2. the recorder's six `except Exception` guards ->       2

The fifth node - "an undeclared retention root leaves the live path untaped" -
has no revert by construction: it asserts an INVARIANT (there is no default
root), and the only change that could redden it is inventing one.  It is written
as a full mixed meeting followed by a grep of the whole tree for `.pcm` and
`index.json`, so it fails the moment a default appears.

THE SHAPE, IN ONE PARAGRAPH.  `LiveSessionTapeRecorder(store_or_None)` is the
only tape object the transport holds.  It is constructed ALWAYS - with `None`
when no root is declared - and every method is then a no-op, so "the service
every gate was measured on" is a state of the wiring rather than the absence of
it.  Five call sites: `create` at session create; `append_lane_frame` after the
v2 ingress ack in the frames route; `append_mixed` at
`LiveCompatibilityMixer.admit_available`'s sealed commit, at BOTH the mid-meeting
call and the `final=True` one in stop; `release` beside every
`v2_mixers.release` (six in live_transport plus
`LiveHelperFailureCoordinator._release_registries`); and `reap()` once at
`attach_live_routes`, which is service start.  `create_app` gained
`live_tape_store=None` and `web_cli.py` does not pass it.

THREE DECISIONS, WITH THE REASONING, SO THEY ARE NOT RE-ARGUED.

1. THE TEE IS AFTER THE ACK, NOT BEFORE IT.  The tape records what the session
   ACCEPTED.  A frame the ingress refused is in neither the meeting nor the tape,
   which is the only reading under which the tape and the transcript describe the
   same audio.  The consequence worth stating: a replay the ingress re-acks
   inside LIVE_V2_REPLAY_ACK_WINDOW does reach the tape, and lands as the
   appender's `duplicate` - because placement is by capture timestamp, an outbox
   retry cannot double-write.  That is gate C's property arriving for free at the
   wired path rather than being re-implemented at it.

2. THE TAPE'S LIFECYCLE IS THE MIXED TRACK'S LIFECYCLE.  `release` is paired with
   `v2_mixers.release`, not with `access.release_session`, because once the mixer
   is gone no further mixed audio can exist for that session and a tape kept open
   past it could only accumulate lane frames with no mixed track.  THE SITE THAT
   MAKES THIS LOAD-BEARING IS THE COORDINATOR'S: a helper lease expiry is the
   USUAL terminal path on the real hosts - F1's only terminal line was
   `helper_lease_expired`, and F3's was too - and a tape left open there stays in
   the store's active set, is skipped by every reap (`reap` unions
   `active_session_ids` with `self._tapes`), and outlives its TTL for the life of
   the process.  That is the immortal tape ADR-0003 D6 exists to prevent, reached
   by the path a clean stop never takes.

3. THE NEVER-RAISES RULE IS ENFORCED AT THE RECORDER, NOT AT EIGHT CALL SITES.
   `LiveSessionTape` already promises that no FRAME raises; the store's own
   create/release/reap touch a filesystem and can.  An OSError escaping
   `POST /frames` is a 500, i.e. a meeting ended by the substrate ADR-0003 D5 was
   written to protect - the third amendment's rule violated by its own remedy.
   Each swallow logs one WARNING naming the action (create/lookup/append/release/
   reap) and the error, so a tape that silently vanishes is never indistinguish-
   able from one that was never enabled.  The route node proves the whole meeting
   - four frames, a mixed commit and a clean stop - survives a store whose every
   method raises ENOSPC.

WHAT WAS LEARNED.

1. A STOP WITH QUEUED WORK NEEDS A DEADLINE, AND ITS 409 READS LIKE A TAPE BUG.
   The first two route nodes failed at `stop` with 409 `live service stop
   deadline expired with unresolved work` on `{"deadline": 0.0}` - in BOTH the
   taped and the untaped run, which is what proved it had nothing to do with the
   tape.  The pre-existing mixing test never stops, so nothing in the suite had
   paid this before.  `{"deadline": 5.0}` is the fix and it is recorded in the
   fence.

2. THE COORDINATOR ALREADY HAD THE RIGHT SEAM AND IT COST NOTHING TO USE IT.
   `LiveHelperFailureCoordinator` takes its registries as `_SessionReleaseRegistry`
   - a structural protocol whose whole content is `release(session_id)`.  Naming
   the recorder's method `release` (mirroring the store's vocabulary) made it
   satisfy that protocol with no new type, no new protocol and a one-line
   constructor change.  Vocabulary chosen to match an existing seam is cheaper
   than vocabulary chosen to read well in isolation.

3. THE MIXED TRACK'S TIMESTAMP IS IN THE DIAGNOSTICS, NOT IN THE FRAME.  The
   `AudioFrame` a mix commits carries a runtime SEQUENCE; only
   `LiveMixDiagnostics.start_timestamp_ns` says where in wall-clock time the
   interval begins, and that is the entire basis on which the tape places it.
   Teeing `mixed.frame` alone would have produced a tape that looks right and is
   silently arrival-ordered - the exact defect iteration 19's first revert exists
   to catch, arriving through the wiring instead of through the appender.

BLOCKERS: none for this iteration.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP.  The declaration surface, in one iteration, inside
ops/ + moss_transcribe_diarize/ + tests/: an `ops/moss-live.env` key for the
retention root plus the TTL and the cap, threaded through `web_cli.py` to
`create_app(live_tape_store=...)`.  Candidate 63's rule governs all three - a
free deployed parameter is STATED by the deployment, never defaulted by a tool -
and ADR-0003 D3 already fixes the one value a tool may choose (TTL 0).  Until it
lands the deployed service still cannot write a byte, which is why it was
deliberately not bundled here: the wiring is provable offline, the declaration
changes what a running host does.  Step 3 (the retrospective sweep) is what makes
the tape pay, and it is the first Phase N item that needs the tape wired.

RUN 20260729-025318 - ITERATION 21

decided retention (ADR-0003), built the writer (`live_tape.py`) and put it on the
live path (`LiveSessionTapeRecorder`, five call sites) - but `web_cli.py` passed

step 2 code-complete.  No authorization needed: step 2 is inside the already-open
Phase N, and candidate 63's rule (a free deployed parameter is STATED by the
deployment, never defaulted by a tool) plus ADR-0003 D2/D3/D4 already fix every

RED-BEFORE - FIVE SEMANTIC REVERTS, 14 OF THE 15 NEW NODES, run and restored
in-iteration (originals copied to /tmp/i21-redbefore, restored, `git diff --stat`
shows additions only):
  A  drop `create_app(live_tape_store=live_tape_store)`   -> 1 red
     (test_the_declared_store_reaches_the_application)

The one node no revert reddens is
`test_the_cli_builds_no_store_when_no_root_is_declared`: it is the off-by-default

THE SHAPE, IN ONE PARAGRAPH.  Three keys - MOSS_LIVE_RETENTION_ROOT,
MOSS_LIVE_RETENTION_MAX_BYTES, MOSS_LIVE_RETENTION_TTL_SECONDS - which
`ops/start-web.sh` translates into `--live-retention-root`,
`--live-retention-max-bytes` and `--live-retention-ttl-seconds`, which
`web_cli._live_tape_store` turns into `LiveSessionTapeStore.declared(...)` or
`None`, handed to `create_app(live_tape_store=...)`.  Declaring the root is the
whole switch.

FOUR DECISIONS, WITH THE REASONING.

1. THE TRACKED TEMPLATE SHIPS THE KEYS COMMENTED OUT, NOT AS `REPLACE_WITH_`
   PATHS.  Every other live key in `moss-live.env.example` is required, so the
   template reads as a form to fill in - and a form whose verbatim use turns
   meeting-audio retention on would make a privacy posture a side effect of
   copying a file.  ADR-0003 D2 says retention is opt-in and off by default;
   "off by default" has to be a property of the tracked artifact, not of an
   operator's restraint.  Two nodes hold it: one asserts the template used
   verbatim emits no `--live-retention` flag at all, and one asserts the
   COMMENTED keys are nonetheless read by the adapter - because the existing
   `test_live_profile_sets_only_variables_the_adapter_reads` walks
   `read_env_file`, which skips comments, so a typo in a commented key would
   otherwise be invisible in exactly the file whose job is to be readable.

2. A CAP OR A TTL WITH NO ROOT IS REFUSED, AT BOTH LAYERS.  The failure is
   asymmetric and only one half is safe: retention off when an operator believes
   it is off is fine, and retention off when they believe audio is being kept is
   the "known but not shown" class this project has now paid for in candidates
   57, 59, 60 and the fourth amendment.  The adapter refuses it and names the
   missing key; `_live_tape_store` refuses it and names the flags that were
   stated.  The set-but-empty root is refused separately by the adapter's own
   `${VAR+set}` discipline, which start-web.sh already states in its own words:
   "a variable a profile sets to nothing is a typo in that profile, not a request
   for the default, and it must be refused rather than absorbed."

3. THE TTL IS OPTIONAL AND UNSTATED MEANS 0; THE CAP IS REQUIRED.  Not a new
   decision - ADR-0003 D3 and `LiveSessionTapeStore.declared`'s own docstring
   already ruled it, and this change's job was to mirror it at the env layer
   rather than invent a second rule.  Zero is the only value a tool may choose,
   because at zero the PRD's "no raw audio is persisted" clause still holds
   literally at every boundary an operator can observe after a meeting; a
   positive TTL is the deployment stating that meeting audio outlives the
   meeting.  The cap has no safe default in either direction (0 would mean
   "never tape", unbounded is the D4(3) runaway), so it is required whenever a
   root is declared.

4. `runs_directories=(args.runs_dir,)` IS WHAT MAKES D4(3) REACHABLE AT ALL.
   `declared()` refuses a root that shares a filesystem with a runs tree, but it
   can only check the runs trees it is handed, and the wiring is the only place
   that knows one: the live service's own `--runs-dir`.  On the deployment host
   that is `/mnt/d/.../live-runs`, the same 9p filesystem the batch runs tree
   lives on - so passing the one directory this process is told about is exactly
   what refuses a root whose runaway tape would answer 507 to a BATCH upload
   without ever touching the batch service (`server.py:447`, free space below
   `2 x content_length + 512 MB`).  The typed `LiveTapeRootError` is deliberately
   NOT caught: that is the reason it is an exception (N-tape decision 2 - a root
   that cannot hold audio safely must stop the service starting with retention
   enabled rather than silently disabling it), and `_live_runtime_factory` right
   above it already sets the precedent of letting the manifest's own typed error
   surface unaltered.

WHAT WAS LEARNED.

1. THE ADAPTER'S "THE SWITCH IS THE WHOLE SWITCH" CONTRACT DECIDED WHERE THE
   RETENTION BLOCK GOES.  `test_disabled_live_mode_generates_no_live_flag_
   whatever_else_is_set` deliberately asserts that `MOSS_LIVE_ENABLED=0` absorbs
   every other live key without complaint.  So a retention key set while live is
   disabled is tolerated, not refused - and that is the safe direction of the
   asymmetry in decision 2, so following the existing contract cost nothing.  The
   retention block therefore lives inside the live case, with no out-of-block
   check to keep in step with it.

2. A COMMENTED-OUT DECLARATION NEEDS ITS OWN TEST, AND THE SUITE ALREADY TOLD ME
   SO.  The existing template test only ever sees uncommented keys.  Choosing to
   ship the opt-in as comments therefore moved three keys out of the coverage the
   file was built to give - which would have been a silent regression in the one
   artifact whose whole purpose is to be copied correctly.  `commented_keys()` is
   nine lines and closes it.  The general form: when a change moves something out
   of an existing test's field of view, the change owes that test's guarantee
   somewhere else.

3. THE TESTS DRIVE `parse_args` THROUGH `sys.argv`, NOT A HAND-BUILT NAMESPACE.
   A `Namespace(live_retention_root=...)` built in the test would pass even if the
   flag were spelled differently in the parser - and the flag spelling is the
   contract `ops/start-web.sh` has to match.  Driving the real parser means a
   renamed flag fails here rather than on the deployment host.

BLOCKERS: none for this iteration.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO.  The deployed host still declares no root: `ops/moss-live.env`
is host-local and untracked, nothing on the server was touched, and the tracked
template's keys are comments - so the live service remains byte-for-byte the one
every gate measured and the PRD's "no raw audio is persisted" clause holds
unchanged.  No manifest or finalizer treatment either, on purpose: the retention
root is a HOST fact like the TLS key path, not a provider config the manifest hash
covers.  ADR-0003's "what the clause becomes for a future hygiene check" is the
two-form test to run at the moment an operator first fills the keys in.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP.  Phase N step 3, the retrospective sweep - the first item
the tape actually pays for, and the one ADR-0002 says the album needs or live
accuracy diverges from whole-file (the "terminal-state failure if shipped alone"
clause).  It is inside the open Phase N and needs no host and no operator: re-VAD
/ re-embed / re-cluster the tape seeded by live labels, never re-ASR, versioned
silent corrections.  The accuracy harness from iteration 16 is the instrument that
can measure live->file convergence once the sweep exists, which is the half of
ADR-0002's acceptance bar the repo still cannot answer.

RUN 20260729-025318  ITERATION 22  -  PHASE N STEP 3: THE RETROSPECTIVE SWEEP'S
ENGINE (N-sweep).  ADR-0002's rewrite half, in source, pure and unwired.
================================================================================

TARGET.  The highest-leverage open item in context.md: Phase N step 3, named by
iteration 21's own recommended next step and by ADR-0002's implementation order
(album -> tape -> sweep -> batch unification).  ADR-0002 classifies the album
alone as "a terminal-state failure if shipped alone" - without retrospective
rewrites, live accuracy repeats the sibling project's <80 % divergence.  The
album (iteration 15) fixes what a label is matched AGAINST; only a sweep can fix
a label already written down.  Chosen off no other list: prd.md's "Phase N is
SUPERSEDED by ADR-0002" section keeps Phase N authorized and names step 3.

Re-read at the start of the iteration, per the standing hazard: prd.md's tail is
unchanged at 0456177 (the ADR-0002 supersession) and `git log -8` shows no new
operator commit since iteration 21.  Nothing was frozen or unfrozen under me.

FILES TOUCHED (5; NONE under macos/, NONE under ops/):
  moss_transcribe_diarize/app/live_identity_sweep.py   NEW, the engine
  tests/test_live_identity_sweep.py                    NEW, 40 nodes
  moss_transcribe_diarize/app/live_identity.py         matcher extracted
  moss_transcribe_diarize/app/live_identity_album.py   cosine + centroid + exemplars()
  moss_transcribe_diarize/app/live_provider_bundle.py  _cosine_similarity now a wrapper
  scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}          this record

VALIDATION.
  python3 -m pytest tests/test_live_identity_sweep.py -q  -> 40 passed, 3.5 s
  python3 -m pytest -q                                    -> 758 passed, 2 skipped,
                                                             368 subtests, 71.50 s
                                                             (718 -> 758, +40)
  The accuracy harness re-measured through the extracted matcher:
    album 93.4 / min 92.2 ; overwrite 72.0 / min 55.7
  - identical to iteration 16's recorded numbers, which is the real proof the
  extraction is behaviour-preserving.  A green unit suite would not have been.

FOUR DECISIONS, MADE EXPLICITLY BEFORE THE PATCH.

1. A SWEEP RE-MATCHES RETAINED EVIDENCE; IT NEVER RE-HEARS AUDIO.  ADR-0002's
   prose says the sweep "re-embed[s]/re-cluster[s] the assembled tape".  Its
   MEASURED gate B says a sweep costs ~0.1 ms at 600 s and <10 ms extrapolated
   to three hours, while the same document measures embedding at 332-343 ms PER
   UNIT.  Those two numbers cannot both describe re-embedding: a 600 s meeting
   holds hundreds of units, so re-embedding it is minutes, not 0.1 ms.  The run
   that PASSED the gate therefore re-matched the vectors the live path had
   already computed, against the album as it stood at sweep time.  Implement the
   measured thing, not the prose.  It is also what the album's own thesis says
   out loud - "the album is the compressed context handed forward: later
   processing never re-hears earlier audio".
   THE HONEST COST, recorded so no convergence number is over-read: a sweep can
   repair an ASSIGNMENT (this voice was labelled as the wrong speaker) and cannot
   repair a SEGMENTATION (the span's local diarization split two voices wrongly,
   or the evidence floor skipped a unit).  ADR-0002 section 7 carries the
   identical caveat - "in-span local diarization assumed correct" - so gate B's
   convergence was measured under exactly this limit.
   CONSEQUENCE THE LOOP MUST CARRY: step 3 does NOT pay for step 2's tape.  The
   tape's nearer value is crash/resume and being the substrate for the later
   re-VAD sweep; iteration 21's "the first item the tape pays for" was too
   optimistic and this entry supersedes it.

2. THE MATCHER IS NOW ONE FUNCTION, CALLED BY BOTH PATHS.  `assign_speakers` was
   extracted from `BoundedCausalIdentityPreparer._assign` (with
   `_match_rejection_reason`) into a module-level function in live_identity.py;
   the method now delegates.  A sweep that re-implemented the matcher would emit
   "corrections" that are a second opinion from a second implementation - the
   exact hazard tests/live_identity_accuracy.py was built to rule out, and the
   one ADR-0002's own prototype fell into (its 98.5 % came from a re-implemented
   matcher).  Same argument for the geometry: `cosine_similarity` and
   `duration_weighted_centroid` now live once, in live_identity_album.py, and
   `_cosine_similarity` in live_provider_bundle is a four-line wrapper that keeps
   its two older typed admission errors verbatim so nothing about the deployed
   provider's contract moves.

3. THREE RULES BOUND WHAT A SWEEP MAY CHANGE, each because a correction can be
   worse than the mistake.
   (a) It never invents a canonical speaker - births are a live decision under
       the 16-speaker cap, and a sweep that could birth would put labels in the
       transcript no live reader ever saw.
   (b) It never removes a label it cannot replace (J2: identity answers *who*,
       never *whether*).  This one is enforced by the TYPE -
       `SweepCorrection.canonical_speaker` is non-optional - so an erasure is
       unrepresentable rather than merely unimplemented.  Recorded honestly: the
       node asserting it is green by construction and no revert reddens it.
   (c) A move must beat the incumbent's own score by `min_match_margin`.
       MEASURED REDUNDANT at the deployed 0.35 / 0.1: the production matcher
       already refuses to assign unless the winner beats every rival by the
       margin, and the incumbent is a rival, so KEPT_BELOW_MARGIN never fires
       there.  The first draft's test for it was unfalsifiable and was replaced
       by one asserting the PROPERTY over real corrections.  The guard is kept
       for a deployment stating a margin above its own match floor, where the
       matcher's guarantee stops covering the incumbent.

4. A MERGE IS A STRONGER CLAIM THAN A MATCH, SO IT NEEDS STRONGER EVIDENCE.  Two
   album centroids at or above 0.70 (ADR-0002's threshold) are one voice born
   twice.  A merge requires an ADMITTED bank on BOTH sides - a provisional
   stand-in is one sub-admission fragment, and letting a fragment collapse two
   speakers would re-open the door the album closed - matches on the DURATION-
   WEIGHTED CENTROID OVER THE UNION of the exemplars (not the mean of two
   centroids: the exemplars carry the seconds that weight them), and leaves the
   id with the most admitted speech standing, so birth order never decides
   identity.  Chains are transitive-closed by union-find: 0 deg and 50 deg are
   0.643 apart and do not merge alone, but through 25 deg they are one voice.
   THIS IS THE FIRST MECHANISM IN THE REPO THAT CAN REDUCE THE CANONICAL SPEAKER
   COUNT, i.e. it can heal candidate 55's fragmentation retrospectively without
   touching births.  It cannot buy back the capacity itself.

TWO PROPERTIES THE SUITE STATES RATHER THAN HOPES FOR.  The sweep is
deterministic (same ledger + album -> identical revision), and applying a
revision leaves NOTHING for the next sweep to correct - convergence, not
oscillation.  Merges do repeat on a second sweep, and that is honest: the album
still holds both speakers until something merges the ALBUM, which is the wiring
step's job, and the repeated claim is the revision saying so.

THE LEDGER'S BOUND IS MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED.  One 256-dimensional float32
vector costs 1104 bytes as an array("f"); the same values as a Python tuple cost
8232 (measured with sys.getsizeof, floats included).  At SWEEP_LEDGER_MAX_UNITS
20 000 the ledger holds ~22 MB, against 165 MB for the tuple form - which is why
storage is array("f") and why `spans()` is an iterator rather than a list.  F3's
real 17-minute soak committed 443 spans in 1029 s = 0.43 spans/s, so three hours
is ~4650 spans and, at the two-speaker spans that meeting produced, under 10 000
units.  The cap is therefore ~2x a three-hour meeting.
A FULL LEDGER REFUSES NEW UNITS RATHER THAN EVICTING OLD ONES - the opposite of
a cache, deliberately.  A sweep's value is correcting the EARLY, low-quality
decisions against a LATER, better album, so the oldest units have the most left
to gain.  It is also live_tape's rule, and a project that answers "what does a
cap do" two different ways has two contracts to keep in step.

RED-BEFORE - TEN SEMANTIC REVERTS, 20 OF THE 40 NODES, run and restored
in-iteration (originals in /tmp/i22-redbefore, restored and verified byte-equal;
`git diff --stat` shows additions only):
   1  `_union(parent, left, right)` -> `pass`                          -> 6 red
   2  leader `min(members, key=(-duration, id))` -> `min(members)`      -> 2 red
   3  `union.extend(banks[speaker])` -> `pass`                          -> 13 red
   4  `ambiguous = True` -> count + `continue`                          -> 1 red
   5  `if unit.local_speaker in unscored:` -> `if False:`               -> 1 red
   6  the ledger cap check -> `if False:`                               -> 1 red
   7  `entry.canonical_speaker = correction...` -> `pass`               -> 2 red
   8  `duration_weighted_centroid(bank)` -> `... or album.reference(s)` -> 1 red
   9  `_finite_float32`'s `if not values:` -> `if False:`               -> 1 red
  10  `reference = album.reference(speaker)` -> `None`                  -> 1 red
Revert 3 is OVER-BROAD and is recorded as such: dropping the union empties every
group's reference, not just a merged one, so it reddens 13 nodes and evidences

record/replace/refuse parametrisation and the constructive invariants
(never-invents, never-removes, determinism, the empty revision) - recorded
rather than manufactured.

WHAT WAS LEARNED.

1. A GUARD THAT CANNOT FIRE IS A TEST THAT CANNOT FAIL, AND THE TEST FOUND IT.
   The margin guard's first node was written to assert KEPT_BELOW_MARGIN and it
   failed for a reason that had nothing to do with the margin - the two
   references it used were 0.94 apart and merged.  Fixing the fixture would have
   produced a node that merely re-asserted the matcher's own rule.  The general
   form, third time this loop has paid for it: when a node is hard to construct,
   ask whether the behaviour it wants is reachable at all before making the
   fixture more elaborate.

2. TWO NUMBERS IN A DESIGN DOCUMENT CAN CONTRADICT ITS PROSE, AND THE NUMBERS
   WIN.  ADR-0002's sweep description and its measured sweep cost cannot both be
   true.  The loop's standing rule - measured beats asserted - resolved a scope
   question that would otherwise have cost an iteration of re-embedding work
   that no gate asked for.

3. AN OVER-BROAD REVERT IS STILL EVIDENCE, BUT ONLY FOR WHAT IT ISOLATES.
   Reverting the union changed 13 nodes; reporting it as "13 nodes prove the
   union rule" would be false.  Reported as one node's evidence plus a note.

BLOCKERS: none for this iteration.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO.  Nothing calls sweep().  There is no cadence, no ledger on
the live path, no transcript revision, no versioned rewrite, and the album is
never itself merged.  The deployed service is untouched - the payload is offline
Python with no route, no flag and no env key - and the branch's existing
unmerged-source condition is unchanged (offline probes have not spoken for the
deployed 42abc5a since iteration 15 and still do not).

WHAT "WHOLE-FILE" MEANS HERE, DECIDED AND STATED RATHER THAN DRESSED UP.  The
file answer the transcript converges TO is the same album engine run
non-causally, which is precisely what the session-end sweep computes.  That is
ADR-0002 step 4's own end state (batch Tier B unified onto this engine), not a
stand-in for it - so it is the right target, and it also means the convergence
half is true BY CONSTRUCTION and says nothing on its own.  The alternative
considered and rejected was a hand-rolled agglomerative clusterer as an
"independent" oracle: it would have been a second implementation issuing a
second opinion, which is the exact hazard N-sweep decision 2 (one matcher, both
paths) and this harness were built to rule out.  What carries the weight instead
is that BOTH numbers are scored against GROUND TRUTH: `live_accuracy` is the
label a reader saw when the span committed, `accuracy` the label standing at the
end.  A rewriter that churned labels without improving them would show a large
`rewritten_share` and a flat `accuracy`, and the node would fail.

FOUR FINDINGS, TWO OF WHICH REFUTE WHAT ITERATION 22 EXPECTED.

1. THE SWEEP IS WORTH +5.82 pp AND CLEARS ADR-0002's OWN WHOLE-FILE FIGURE.
   99.26 % mean against the ADR's gate-A 98.5 %, and >= 98.48 % on every meeting,
   from rewriting 4-8 % of eligible speech.  Step 3 is measured, not asserted.

2. THE MERGE FIRES ZERO TIMES.  Iteration 22 landed it as candidate 55's
   retrospective cure and named that expectation in context.md; it is wrong, for
   a STRUCTURAL reason rather than an incidental one.  A merge requires an
   ADMITTED exemplar bank on both sides (N-sweep decision 4), and the canonical
   speakers a saturated capacity mints are born from sub-admission fragments that
   never earn one.  Measured directly by instrumenting the album at session end:
   of the 16 canonical speakers minted, the album ends holding only 3-6, of which
   2-3 are banked; the banked centroids sit at 0.192 / 0.269 / 0.427 pairwise
   maxima against the 0.70 merge threshold - i.e. they are genuinely different
   voices and SHOULD NOT merge.  So every point of the gain is RE-MATCHING.
   The node asserts merges == 0 in falsifiable form: if a parameter change ever
   makes one fire, it fails and the finding is re-measured, not inherited.

3. THE SWEEP ERASES CANDIDATE 55's 4.5 pp FROM THE FINAL TRANSCRIPT ENTIRELY.
   Capped-and-swept 99.26 equals uncapped-and-swept 99.26 (|delta| < 0.005), and
   capped-and-swept already beats uncapped-UNswept 98.74.  The 16-speaker bound
   still costs the LIVE transcript 5.30 pp (93.44 vs 98.74).  Candidate 55 is
   therefore RE-PRICED, not closed: it is a LATENCY of labelling, not a permanent
   loss of it.  Authorizing a fix for it is now a decision about what a reader
   sees DURING a meeting, and it should be weighed against wiring the sweep,
   which is already authorized and costs no further permission.

4. THE CADENCE IS NEARLY FREE OF EFFECT.  A 600 s interval (one mid-meeting sweep
   plus the session-end one) gives 99.22 % against 60 s's 99.26 %.  The value is
   in the SESSION-END sweep, not in the pacing.  SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS 60 buys a
   reader earlier corrections, not a better ending - worth knowing before the
   wiring step argues about cadence cost against the GPU.

AND THE CONVERGENCE PROPERTY IS ASSERTED ON REAL MEETINGS.  `residual_corrections`
is one extra sweep run AFTER the applied session-end one, deliberately not
applied; it is 0 on all eight.  test_live_identity_sweep already proves
determinism over constructed evidence - what this adds is the cadence failure that
suite cannot see: two near-equal references trading a unit back and forth, every
trade a visible transcript revision a reader watches happen.

paces the sweep.  It deliberately does NOT rewrite a transcript; see WHAT THIS
DOES NOT DO.

  moss_transcribe_diarize/app/live_identity_sweep.py   +LiveIdentitySweeper, batch scoring
  moss_transcribe_diarize/app/live_provider_bundle.py  the two feeding points, the factory

  tests/test_live_identity_sweep.py                    +14 nodes (40 -> 54)

VALIDATION.  `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` -> 784 passed / 2 skipped / 368
subtests in 74.81 s (was 764 / 2 / 368 in 78.34 s; +20 nodes, and the suite got
FASTER because the accuracy harness runs 8 x 11 sweeps through the new scorer).
The two skips are the pre-existing Python-3.10 contract at
tests/test_large_upload.py:155,175.  Swift untouched, so 158 stands.

FIVE DECISIONS, EACH RECORDED BECAUSE EACH COULD HAVE GONE THE OTHER WAY.

1. WHERE THE LEDGER LIVES - iteration 23's open question (a).  With the album, in
   `WeSpeakerLiveEvidenceProvider`.  It is the only object in the live path that
   ever holds a vector, and the album and the ledger are fed by the same event;
   splitting them would create two feeding paths that can disagree about who
   spoke.  The sweeper (ledger + cadence + config + merge threshold) is its own
   object so the *scheduling* question stays separable from the *retention* one.

2. A UNIT IS RETAINED TWICE, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN, NOT AN ACCIDENT.  The album
   only ever hears an assignment the live path MADE; the ledger hears every unit
   the encoder embedded.  So a unit is recorded unlabelled when its vector is
   computed and re-recorded carrying its canonical speaker when the next span's
   preparation reconciles it - `SweepLedger.record` answers `replaced` for the
   second and the unit count does not move.  The reason for the wider rule is in
   the ledger's own docstring: an ABSTAINED span never reconciles, and an
   abstained span is exactly the one a later album has the most to say about.
   Retaining only what was already labelled would make the sweep unable to
   improve the spans the live path found hardest.

3. THE CADENCE FIRES BEFORE THE CURRENT SPAN'S EVIDENCE IS RETAINED, and the
   meeting time it is paced by is the span's START.  A sweep that could see the
   span being prepared would propose a label for it before the live path had
   assigned one, and every one of those would be a "correction" to a transcript
   nobody had read yet.  Because the reconcile runs first, at cadence time every
   span except the one in flight is already settled.

4. MEETING TIME, NEVER WALL TIME.  `SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` is a distance along
   the transcript (a sample count divided by 16000), so a meeting that arrives in
   a burst after an outage is swept the same number of times as one that arrived
   smoothly - and, unlike a wall clock, it cannot step backwards.  That is the
   Duration-vs-timestamp contract and candidate 56's entire cause.  The next
   deadline is computed FROM THE TIME REACHED, not by adding an interval to the
   previous one, so a long gap schedules one sweep rather than a burst of them
   catching up over time in which no evidence was retained.  A non-finite or
   non-numeric meeting time returns None and never raises.

5. THE BUNDLE CANNOT BUILD AN ALBUM WITHOUT A SWEEPER.  ADR-0002 classes the
   album shipped without the retrospective sweep as a TERMINAL-STATE FAILURE, so
   a code path that could produce one without the other would be a way to ship
   the documented failure by omission.  `_identity_evidence_provider`'s
   `identity_config` is therefore REQUIRED, not defaulted: there is no argument
   list that yields an album and no sweeper.  The new `_identity_preparer` builds
   the config once and hands it to both halves, so a sweeper holding its own
   `LiveIdentityConfig` - candidate 63 one layer down, measured at one
   calibration and revised at another - is unwritable.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGED THE PATCH.  ADR-0002 gate B reports a sweep at
~0.1 ms for 600 s and "<10 ms extrapolated to 3 h".  Measured here on production
code, at F3's own real shape (443 spans, 886 units, 16 canonical speakers, 256
dimensions), scoring pair by pair through `cosine_similarity`:

    F3 17 min   886 units   295 ms
    1 h        3126 units  1032 ms
    3 h        9380 units  3098 ms      <-- LONGER THAN THE 2.5 s SPAN CAP

The sweep runs INLINE on the serial canonical pump, inside `provider.score()`
inside `prepare_work_item`.  A 3.1 s stall once a minute on that queue is the
same shape as candidate 50's runaway decode, which D-c exists to bound - and it
would land on ~4 % of spans, right at the PRD's p95 boundary.  The ADR's figure
is off by ~300x, so this is the second time its prose and its measurements
disagree (iteration 22 ruled the first one: take the measured value).

SO THE SCOPE WAS WIDENED, and prompt.md's own rule is the justification -
"widen scope only when the focused result justifies it".  `_score_span` now
scores a whole span against a reference matrix built ONCE PER SWEEP rather than
once per pair.  Same numbers, measured:

    F3 17 min   295 ms -> 39 ms      (7.5x)
    1 h        1032 ms -> 125 ms     (8.3x)
    3 h        3098 ms -> 366 ms     (8.5x)

366 ms once per 60 s of meeting is ~0.6 % duty on the pump and well inside one
span's budget.  The batch path is an OPTIMISATION and is provably
indistinguishable: it refuses exactly what `cosine_similarity` refuses (a
dimension mismatch, a vector with no length, a non-finite result), it decides
that for the WHOLE SPAN so a span is never scored half one way and half the
other, and it falls back to the untouched scalar rule otherwise.  The proof is
not an assertion: the eight-meeting accuracy harness still measures 99.26 % mean
/ 98.48 % min swept and 93.44 / 72.0 unswept, unchanged to the hundredth, and
`residual_corrections` is still 0 on every meeting.

RED-BEFORE - NINE SEMANTIC REVERTS, run and restored in-iteration (originals in
/tmp/i24-redbefore; `git diff --stat` after restoring shows additions only):
  1  no unlabelled retention at score time                     -> 5 red
  2  the cadence moved AFTER this span's evidence is retained  -> 2 red
  3  a reconciled assignment never reaches the ledger          -> 3 red
  4  a sweep never applies its own revision to the ledger      -> 2 red
  5  the bundle builds an album with no sweeper                -> 1 red
  6  an untrustworthy meeting time is not guarded              -> 1 red

  9  the batch path does not refuse a vector with no length    -> 1 red
Revert 3 was run twice.  The FIRST run reddened only 2 nodes and left
`test_a_reconciled_assignment_reaches_the_ledger_as_well_as_the_album` green -

red-before discipline exists to catch: a green node measuring the wrong cause.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO - so a green suite is not mistaken for step 3 being done.
  * NOTHING CONSUMES A REVISION.  `sweep_now` applies it to the LEDGER (which is
    what makes the next sweep converge rather than re-propose forever) and
    returns it, and the caller drops it.  No transcript is rewritten, no portal
    shows a correction, no reader sees anything change.  Step 3's user-visible
    half is the next iteration.
  * THERE IS NO SESSION-END SWEEP.  Iteration 23 measured that the session-end
    sweep is where essentially all the value is (600 s cadence gives 99.22 %
    against 60 s's 99.26 %), and it needs a per-session teardown hook the
    provider does not have.  It belongs with "who applies a revision", because
    both are the same question about ownership.
  * THE FINAL SPAN OF A MEETING STAYS UNLABELLED IN THE LEDGER.  A span is
    labelled when the NEXT span's preparation reconciles it, and the last span
    has no next.  Harmless today (nothing reads the ledger's labels but the
    sweep, and no sweep runs after it); it must be closed by the session-end
    hook feeding the final identity snapshot through `_reconcile_committed_
    vectors` BEFORE the final sweep, or that sweep would issue a spurious
    "labelled" correction for a span the live path had already labelled.
  * THE ALBUM IS NEVER ITSELF MERGED, unchanged from iteration 22.
  * The deployed service is unaffected in behaviour: the album, the matcher and
    every published label are untouched, which is what the accuracy harness's
    unchanged 93.44 / 72.0 proves.  The branch's unmerged-source condition is
    what it was - offline probes have not spoken for the deployed 42abc5a since
    iteration 15 and still do not.

BLOCKERS: none for this iteration.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP.  APPLY A REVISION TO THE TRANSCRIPT - the user-visible
half of step 3, and the last thing between Phase N and a gate.  What has to be
decided before the patch, all three visible from the code now:
  (a) WHERE THE REWRITE LIVES.  A committed span's label is baked into its
      transcript string as a DISPLAY label (`[0.11][S03]words[1.75]`), the local
      speaker is gone by then, and `CanonicalCommit.prefix_hash` chains the
      committed list.  So either the session retains a per-span local->canonical
      map (it is already in `preparation.proposed_snapshot.diagnostics`), or the
      revision is carried beside the transcript and applied at render.  The hash
      chain is the argument for the second: it records what was SAID, and a
      living document's corrections are a different fact.
  (b) THE SESSION-END SWEEP AND ITS RECONCILE, per the third bullet above.
  (c) WHAT A READER SEES when 4-8 % of the speech they have already read changes
      speaker.  ADR-0002 promises a "living document"; nothing in the portal
      shows a version of a label yet.

THE THREE DECISIONS ITERATION 24 LEFT OPEN, ANSWERED.

(a) WHERE THE REWRITE LIVES - BESIDE THE TRANSCRIPT, NOT IN IT.  `CanonicalCommit`
    gains `revised_transcript`, `None` until something corrects that span.
    `transcript` and `prefix_hash` never move.  The argument is the chain: the
    committed transcripts are hashed into `prefix_hash`, so the chain records what
    was SAID, and a living document's corrections are a different fact about the
    same words.  Editing `transcript` would rewrite the meeting under every client
    that verifies the chain.  A reader is shown `revised_transcript || transcript`.

(b) HOW A CORRECTION IS ADDRESSED - BY (SPAN, LOCAL SPEAKER), WHICH MEANT THE
    SESSION HAD TO RETAIN A LABEL TRACK.  A sweep's unit is `(span, local
    speaker)`; a committed span carries canonical DISPLAY labels (or `S00`), and
    the local speaker is gone by then.  Addressing by displayed label cannot work,
    and the reason is exactly the case that matters most: an ABSTAINED span
    displays `S00` for every one of its local speakers, and N-sweep-wiring
    decision 2 retains those units precisely because they are the ones a later
    album has the most to say about.  So `LiveSession` now retains, per committed
    span, the decoder's local speaker per published segment (`CanonicalResult
    .local_speakers`, and a new `local_speakers=` on `submit_unlabeled_canonical`).
    The coordinator reads it from the DECODER's transcript - the only place a local
    speaker still exists - and both published renderings walk `span_segments` of
    that same string, so position i here is position i there by construction.  The
    session refuses a track whose length disagrees rather than trusting that
    sentence.  Cost: one short tuple per span against a committed list that is
    already O(meeting).

(c) WHAT A READER SEES - the corrected speaker in place, and a "label revisions: N"
    line that appears only once something has been corrected.  A meeting whose live
    labels stood has nothing to say about revisions; printing "0" invites a reader
    to wonder what went wrong.  The portal change is two lines, because the
    correction is applied server-side into a field the page already renders.

FOUR RULES THAT MAKE A SELF-REWRITING TRANSCRIPT SAFE, each enforced rather than
promised:
  1. THE WORDS CANNOT MOVE.  A span is revised only if re-rendering its own
     committed segments with their own committed labels reproduces the committed
     string BYTE FOR BYTE.  A transcript that does not round-trip keeps everything
     it has and says so by name (`span_does_not_re_render`).  This is why the
     renderer moved into `live_span_bounds` beside `span_segments`: one grammar,
     read and written by one implementation, proved per span instead of assumed.
  2. A SPAN NEVER PUTS TWO OF ITS OWN LOCAL SPEAKERS ON ONE IDENTITY.  The live
     matcher assigns one-to-one; a sweep re-matches unit by unit and can reach that
     state across dispositions.  Publishing it would claim the span's own local
     diarization was wrong - a claim a sweep is explicitly not allowed to make
     (N-sweep decision 1: it re-matches evidence, it never re-hears audio).
     `UNATTRIBUTED_SPEAKER` is exempt: several speakers being nobody in particular
     is the honest state an abstention publishes.
  3. NOTHING RAISES AND NOTHING IS TERMINAL.  Six refusal words, counted and
     returned: span_not_committed, span_has_no_label_track, local_speaker_not_in_
     span, canonical_speaker_unknown, span_does_not_re_render,
     span_labels_would_collide (plus label_unchanged).  They travel to
     `canonical_processed` as `identity_revision_refusals`, because a rewriter
     nobody can audit is worse than no rewriter - and a correction that silently
     evaporates is this project's own "known but not shown" defect in new clothes.
  4. A CLOSED SESSION IS STILL REVISABLE.  Iteration 23 measured that essentially
     all of the accuracy is in the SESSION-END sweep (600 s cadence gives 99.22 %
     against 60 s's 99.26 %), and that sweep necessarily arrives after the last
     span.  A session that stopped accepting corrections when it stopped accepting
     audio would refuse the most valuable one of the meeting.  The version bump is
     what tells a still-polling reader to come back for it.

OWNERSHIP, stated because it is the question 24 could not answer.  The COORDINATOR
applies a revision, because it is the only object holding both halves: the identity
stack, which knows a past minute was labelled wrong, and the session, which owns the
published words.  It asks by name - `take_identity_revision` on the preparer ->
the provider -> `LiveIdentitySweeper.take_revision` - and the capability is OPTIONAL
at every layer for one reason: a stack with no album has no sweeper, has retained
nothing, and has nothing to say about a span it already answered.  That is every
stack this project shipped before ADR-0002 step 3 and every test double.
`take_revision` is separate from `latest_revision` and it EMPTIES: a caller polling
it on every span would otherwise re-publish one correction for the rest of the
meeting.  Only the newest is kept - a sweep re-matches the whole ledger against the
album as it stands, so its revision supersedes every earlier one.

RED-BEFORE - TEN SEMANTIC REVERTS, run and restored in-iteration (originals in
/tmp/i25-redbefore; `git diff` after restoring shows additions only).  Nine of the
ten name a DIFFERENT node; reverts 3 and 4 both name the seam node, honestly:
   1  the portal renders only `item.transcript`                     -> 1 red (portal)
   2  a span is never revisable (the label track is ignored)        -> 7 red (6 session
                                                                       + the seam)
   3  the coordinator never asks for a revision                     -> 1 red (seam)
   4  an abstained span publishes without its local speakers        -> 1 red (seam)
   5  the round-trip guard is dropped                               -> 1 red (the
                                                                       spaced-out node)
   6  two of one span's speakers may become one identity            -> 1 red (collision)
   7  an unknown canonical speaker is labelled anyway               -> 1 red (raises
                                                                       instead of counting)
   8  `take_revision` hands the same revision over forever          -> 1 red (sweep)
   9  a second revision is applied to the published text            -> 1 red (compose)
  10  a PREPARED span publishes without its local speakers          -> 1 red (seam)
Revert 10 exists because the seam's own sweep only corrects the ABSTAINED span, so
the prepared path's track was uncovered until the node asserted it directly.  Same
hazard iteration 24 recorded: a green node can be measuring the wrong cause.

THE SEAM NODE, which is the one that matters.  `test_a_sweep_relabels_an_abstained_
span_in_the_transcript_a_reader_is_holding` drives the real `LiveCoordinator`, real
`LiveSession`, real `BoundedCausalIdentityPreparer`, real `WeSpeakerLiveEvidence
Provider`, real `FingerprintAlbum` and real `LiveIdentitySweeper` through five
two-second spans; only the ONNX forward pass and the GPU decode are scripted.
Span 0 births speaker-0001, span 1 births speaker-0002, span 2 sits equidistant
between them so `ambiguous_identity` abstains and J2 publishes its words under S00,
span 3 is the first speaker again off-centre, and at span 4 the album has heard
enough that the retained evidence re-matches span 2 decisively (0.847 vs 0.707,
margin 0.140 against the deployed 0.1).  The correction lands, and the assertion is
on the transcript a reader holds: committed[2].transcript is still
`[0][S00]who is this[2]` and `revised_transcript` is `[0][S01]who is this[2]`.
Nothing else moved.  No other node in this repository puts the album, the sweeper,
the matcher and the session in one process; each half had been measured alone, and
neither measurement can see whether a correction ever reaches a reader.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO - so a green suite is not mistaken for step 3 being finished.
  * THERE IS STILL NO SESSION-END SWEEP.  The cadence is the only trigger, so the
    meeting's last interval is never swept and the final span is never labelled in
    the ledger (a span is labelled when the NEXT one reconciles it).  That is where
    iteration 23 measured essentially all of the value.  It needs a per-session
    teardown hook the provider does not have, and it must feed the final identity
    snapshot through `_reconcile_committed_vectors` BEFORE the final sweep or that
    sweep issues a spurious `labelled` correction for a span the live path already
    labelled.  `revise_labels` is ready for it: a closed session accepts one.
  * THE ALBUM IS NEVER ITSELF MERGED, unchanged from iterations 22 and 24.  A merge
    correction moves the units; the two album speakers stay separate, so a merge
    repeats on every sweep.  Measured irrelevant so far - the merge fires zero times
    on all eight harness meetings (iteration 23 finding 2).
  * NO EVENT IS EMITTED FOR A REVISION.  The counts ride on `canonical_processed`,
    so a revision is only visible where a span was processed.  A session-end sweep
    will need its own event or the last correction of a meeting is unrecorded.
  * THE DEPLOYED SERVICE IS UNAFFECTED, and the branch's unmerged-source condition
    is what it was: offline probes have not spoken for the deployed 42abc5a since
    iteration 15 and still do not.

BLOCKERS: none for this iteration.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP.  THE SESSION-END SWEEP - the last piece of step 3, and the
one iteration 23 measured to be worth almost all of the accuracy.  Three things are
already decided for it: the hook is per-session teardown (the provider is built per
session by `_identity_preparer_factory`, and the runtime's `stop`/`abort` are the
two places a session ends); the final reconcile must precede the final sweep; and
the transcript half is done, so the hook has somewhere to deliver to.  After that,
Phase N's gate: the accuracy harness plus F1/F2 with the label clause meaningfully
verified, then a merge, push and redeploy - and the redeploy is the one that
regenerates the host manifest at the calibrated 0.35/0.1 (see N-recal).

transcript half (`revise_labels`) was already built to accept a revision on a

supersession (operator commit 0456177), and this is step 3's remaining work.

(+`CoordinatorFinalizeResult`, +`finalize_identity`, +`IDENTITY_FINALIZE_FAILED`,

VALIDATION.  `python3 -m pytest -q` -> **801 passed / 2 skipped / 368 subtests**
in 75.89 s (793/2/368 before; the two skips are the pre-existing 3.10 contract).
Swift untouched and therefore not re-run - the payload contains no `macos/` file.

WHY IT IS A REAL GAP, NOT A REFINEMENT.  The cadence is paced by the NEXT span's
start (`score()` -> `maybe_sweep(meeting_seconds=span.start_sample/16000)`), so:
  * a meeting shorter than one interval is NEVER swept - at the shipped
    SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS of 60 s that is every F1-length canary;
  * every longer meeting's final interval is never swept;
  * and the last span's evidence is retained UNLABELLED for good, because a
    span's vectors acquire their canonical speaker when the FOLLOWING span's
    preparation reconciles them and nothing follows the last one.
The accuracy harness has been measuring the opposite the whole time:
`tests/live_identity_accuracy.py:430` runs `run_sweep(apply=True)` at session end
unconditionally, and that call is inside the 99.26 % mean / 98.48 % min figure
iteration 23 recorded.  So the product could not reach its own gate's number.

THE SHAPE.  One optional capability, asked for by name at each of three layers,
exactly as `take_identity_revision` already is:
  provider  `WeSpeakerLiveEvidenceProvider.finalize_identity(base_snapshot)` -
            `_reconcile_committed_vectors(base_snapshot)` THEN
            `sweeper.sweep_now()`, and it publishes nothing: what the sweep
            produces is left in the sweeper's unconsumed slot exactly as a
            cadence sweep leaves it.
  preparer  `BoundedCausalIdentityPreparer.finalize_identity` - relay only.
  coordinator `LiveCoordinator.finalize_identity()` - hands the stack
            `session.snapshot().identity_snapshot`, then calls the SAME
            `_publish_identity_revision()` every span uses, and returns the five
            revision fields a span already reports.
  runtime   `_finalize_identity_locked` in `stop`, after `_wait_for_drain` and
            before `session.stop`, plus the `identity_finalized` event.

FOUR DECISIONS, RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT RE-ARGUED.
1. THE ORDER IS RECONCILE THEN SWEEP, and it is load-bearing rather than tidy.
   Reversed, the final sweep re-matches the last span while the ledger still has
   it unlabelled, and proposes a `labelled` correction for a span the live path
   had ALREADY labelled correctly - a rewrite that changes nothing, reported as
   if it had changed something (`revise_labels` counts the span as revised and
   bumps the version even when `applied` is 0).  Semantic revert 1 measures it:
   `identity_revision_spans` goes 1 -> 2.
2. THE ABORT PATH DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SWEEP.  An aborted session is terminal,
   a terminal session is not in VIEWABLE_SESSION_STATUSES, and a correction
   published to one reaches no reader - so the only thing a final sweep could add
   there is work on the one path that must do as little as possible.  Stated as a
   rule rather than an omission, and asserted by its own node.
3. NOTHING HERE IS TERMINAL.  A meeting that reached a clean stop has already
   succeeded; an identity stack that raises on the way out costs the transcript
   its last correction and nothing else.  It is counted by NAME
   (`identity_finalize_failed`, merged into the same `identity_revision_refusals`
   map the session's own refusals use) because reporting zero corrections would
   be indistinguishable from a meeting nobody needed to correct.  Third
   amendment's governing rule, applied to teardown.
4. THE EVENT IS RECORDED WHETHER OR NOT ANYTHING CHANGED.  "The last sweep ran
   and found nothing" and "the last sweep never ran" are opposite facts about a
   meeting; the only way to tell them apart after the fact is a line that appears
   either way.  Same five keys as `canonical_processed`'s revision half, so the
   loop's reducers read it with the code they already have.

RED-BEFORE: TWELVE SEMANTIC REVERTS (`/tmp/i26-redbefore/run.py`, applied and
restored in-iteration), every one red, and every one of the 8 new nodes named by
at least one:
   1  sweep before reconcile                          -> 2 red
   2  the final sweep never runs                      -> 2 red
   3  the final reconcile never runs                  -> 3 red
   4  the preparer does not relay                     -> 3 red
   5  the coordinator settles but never publishes     -> 1 red
   6  a stack that cannot settle ends the meeting     -> 1 red
   7  the stop path never settles identity            -> 1 red
   8  the abort path settles it too                   -> 1 red
   9  the event is recorded only when something moved -> 1 red
  10  identity is settled AFTER the session closes    -> 1 red
  11  settled against a snapshot that is not this
      meeting's                                       -> 2 red
  12  the capability is required, not asked for       -> 8 red
TWO OF THEM WERE GREEN ON THE FIRST PASS AND THE NODES WERE WRONG, NOT THE
REVERTS - this is the third consecutive iteration to hit that hazard.
  * Revert 8 was a no-op because `abort` calls `_fail` BEFORE anything else and
    `_finalize_identity_locked` returns early on a terminal session; the honest
    revert inserts the call ahead of `_fail`, and then the node bites.
  * Revert 10 was a no-op because `session_closed` is recorded AFTER the try
    block, so "identity_finalized immediately precedes session_closed" holds
    wherever inside `stop` the finalize sits.  The node now asserts what actually
    separates the two placements: `LiveSession.stop` bumps the version twice on
    its way through, so a finalize that ran BEFORE it necessarily carries a
    strictly lower `snapshot_version` than the close does.  Event ORDER was the
    wrong instrument; the version each event was stamped with is the right one.

  * THE ACCURACY NUMBER IS NOT RE-MEASURED.  The harness already ran a session-end

WHAT I LEARNED (two things, one of which cost a pairing code).
  1. **`payload:` is 113 characters, not 122.**  The retired note says "`tail -1`
     hands the probe a 122-byte string" and the natural reading - that a good
     payload is ~122 bytes - is wrong: 122 is the WHOLE LINE including the 9-char
     `payload: ` prefix.  A sanity guard written from that number rejects a
     CORRECT payload, which is what happened here and cost one mint.  The correct
     extraction `sed -n 's/^payload: //p'` yields exactly **113**.
  2. **`grep` with no match still kills a remote `set -euo pipefail` script**, and
     every check after it silently never runs - the same shape M6c recorded for
     `ls` + pipefail.  On a probe script whose job is to REPORT, drop `set -e` or
     tail every grep with `|| true`; a script that exits early looks exactly like
     a script whose later checks passed.

WHAT I LEARNED (three things).
  1. **A clause can be RED for a reason that is not the system's fault, and the
     reducer cannot tell you which.**  Both of this run's REDs needed the raw
     events to interpret: one is a 150 ms miss with a remedy the PRD already
     names, the other is arithmetic on a 0.03 s span.  This is the fifth time
     the loop has met "a verdict word that does not name what it decides"
     (candidates 57, 59, 61, 62, now 64) - and the first time the honest fix is
     a DECISION rather than a repair.
  2. **A green suite proved a mechanism that a real meeting never reaches.**
     tests/live_identity_accuracy.py has been running a session-end sweep
     unconditionally since iteration 23 and measured 99.26 % from it; iteration
     26 wired the product's own `finalize_identity` to the stop route; and the
     client has never called that route.  Every layer was individually correct
     and covered.  **The only instrument that could see it was a real client
     against a real server** - the same gap H1/K1/53/60 each occupied.
  3. **Two open defects can be the same defect.**  Candidate 60 and "the sweep
     never runs" are one bug with two prices, and the second price is an entire
     ADR acceptance half.  Re-read old candidates against new code before
     ranking them: 60 was filed before step 3 existed.

***What this run proves that F1 could not.*** F1 was 85 s of undisturbed meeting. This is 300 s with a

ARCHIVED BLOCK: CANDIDATE 60 - A CLEAN STOP NEVER REACHES THE SERVER - the full block
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**CANDIDATE 60 — A CLEAN STOP NEVER REACHES THE SERVER (new, iteration 9). This is F3's one RED and
it is a product defect, not a harness artifact.** The PRD clause is *"then clean stop immediately
revokes it"*; measured, the view authority outlived the stop by **29.4 s**.
***Three independent confirmations, so nobody re-derives it.***
1. **The wire.** `grep` of the live service journal for `…/331d8c57…/stop` returns **0**. The
   session's only terminal line is `live helper terminal: … reason=helper_lease_expired lanes=none`
   at epoch 1785298234.27 — **29.4 s after** `t_stop` 1785298204.83, i.e. the 30 s helper lease, not
   the stop.
2. **The snapshot.** The portal poller kept answering 200 with `status=active` for 4 s past the stop
   (last poll t+1026.6 s, version 3646).
3. **The source.** The Swift client builds live URLs in exactly one place, `liveURL(base:sessionID:
   action:)` (`CaptureHTTPTransport.swift:450`), and it has **three** callers: `frames` (`:239`),
   `heartbeat` (`:292`) and the latency probe's snapshot/events (`CaptureLatencyProbe.swift:576`).
   There are only **two** `URLRequest(url:)` sites in the whole client. `CaptureController.stop`
   (`CaptureController.swift:473-496`) stops the source, drains the outbox and returns — it never
   tells the server anything.
***And the server half is already built and already tested.*** `POST /api/live/sessions/{id}/stop`
exists at `live_transport.py:325` and takes a `deadline`; `tests/test_live_api.py:502` is literally
`test_clean_stop_immediately_revokes_view_authority` and passes. **So this is the loop's familiar
class one turn further out:** the behaviour is implemented, contracted and covered on one side of the
seam, and *nothing calls it from the other*. The C1 node proves the route revokes; the Swift suite
proves the controller stops; **no test puts a real client's `stop` in front of a real server**, which
is exactly the gap H1/K1/53 each occupied.
***It was visible in F1 and was not named.*** The F1-green block records "the only terminal line is
`helper_lease_expired lanes=none` **29 s after the run's own stop**" as a curiosity. It was this
defect, in a run whose reducer had no soak clause to test it with.
***Severity, stated so the authorization decision is a decision.*** The exposure is **bounded at
30 s** and self-heals — the lease expires, the session goes terminal and view authority 401s — and no
audio is lost, because the client drains before returning. What fails is the PRD's word *immediately*
and the promise that closing a laptop's meeting closes the browser's access to it. It also costs the
accounting clause its clean read: F3's `accepted − accounted = 14484 samples` is INCONCLUSIVE only
because the session was still active when the last snapshot was taken.
*Tracked product source under `macos/` (and a test under `tests/`), so it is frozen: **needs its own
authorization**. Shape of the fix, not a decision: `CaptureController.stop` gains a transport call
after the final drain, with the same "a publish failure must not stop the meeting ending" rule — a
stop that cannot reach the server must still stop locally, and the lease then does what it does
today.*
