WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. A COMPACTION IS THE ONLY THING THAT RE-READS A LINE NOBODY RE-READS, and that
    is now three passes in a row (4th: seven "not deployed" rows; 5th: nine
    withdrawn claims; 6th: four stale command arguments).  The size problem and
    the staleness problem have the same cause - a block no iteration opens is
    both dead weight and unverified - so a pass taken purely for bytes will keep
    paying for itself in correctness.
 2. THE HONEST NUMBER IS TWO NUMBERS.  The ranges removed 14 730 B and the pass's
    own record cost 3.1 KB back.  Reporting only the -14 730 would have been the
    flattering half of a measurement the loop takes every ten iterations, and the
    next pass plans against it.
 3. AN ANCHOR GUARD IS WHAT MAKES A LINE-NUMBER EDIT SAFE.  Sixteen ranges cut by
    line number from one 2351-line file is exactly the shape that silently
    mis-cuts; requiring each range's first line to still match a recorded
    substring turned two of my own errors (an inverted overlap check and a range
    that started one line late) into refusals before anything was written.
 4. WHAT THE PASS COULD NOT DO IS AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT IT DID.  The fence's
    remaining 40 KB is live instruments - the full gate, live-pipeline-probe's
    recipes, the canary and soak drivers, the reducers, N8c's redeploy template.
    None of it is retirable while F1/F3 are re-runnable and a ninth merge is
    conceivable, which is why the seventh pass's target is measured and named
    below rather than left to be improvised.

BLOCKERS.  None this iteration.  No product source, no test, no ops, no host was
touched; nothing was minted, so there is nothing to roll back.  prd.md's last
commit is still 0456177 - no new authorization exists and none was needed, since
prompt.md names repairing context.md from evidence as a valid iteration.

CANDIDATE 67, NEW, AND IT IS WHY THIS TOOK A MEASUREMENT TO FIND.  The revision
version lives in two places under two names: `canonical_processed` carries

DIFFERENT quantity.  live-pipeline-probe.py:635-637,1080 reads

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. A RE-RUN OF A PASSING-SHAPED GATE IS NOT A FORMALITY.  This run was taken to
    remove staleness and it falsified a candidate the loop had been reasoning
    from for eleven iterations.  The reason is structural: candidate 65 was
    filed from a 319 s meeting and the behaviour it describes is a function of
    MEETING LENGTH.  A claim measured at one scale is a claim about that scale.
 2. THE SAME NAME IN TWO PLACES IS WORSE THAN NO NAME.  `identity_revision_
    version` vs `identity_snapshot_version` cost the loop a real finding for two
    runs, and the failure mode was the exact one iteration 7 named for
    `identity_finalized` and iteration 10 for `storageWrites`: A MISSING FIELD
    READ AS A NEGATIVE MEASUREMENT.  Third instance.  An absent field must
    project as null, never as 0.
 3. FALSIFYING YOUR OWN RECORD DESERVES A CONTROL.  Before withdrawing 65 I
    re-read F2's evidence on the new surface; its zero held.  Without that the
    honest conclusion ("length, not brokenness") would have been
    indistinguishable from "the earlier measurement was wrong", and the loop has
    already been wrong twice in that direction on this exact candidate.

WHAT I FOUND ON THE WAY, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT WAS NOT ON THE CANDIDATE LIST.
`since_seq` is INCLUSIVE server-side (live_service_runtime.events: `event.seq >=
since_seq`), so every poll re-delivers the previous poll's highest event.  The
probe's own ConcurrentViewReader already advances `seq + 1` (:246); the MAIN
loop did not, and counted the repeat as another event.  The tell was sitting in
three reports in plain sight: `session_created: 2` for an event that occurs
exactly once.  The portal - which this probe deliberately mirrors - keeps the
same inclusive request and drops the repeat on the READER side
(live_portal.py:474), so the faithful mirror is to dedupe here and leave the
wire behaviour alone.

FILES TOUCHED.  scripts/ralph-afk/live-pipeline-probe.py (loop tooling only),
scripts/ralph-afk/context.md, scripts/ralph-afk/progress.txt.
NO product source, NO test, NO ops.  `git diff --name-only 7a4f59c HEAD --
':!scripts/ralph-afk'` empty before and after, so every offline probe still
speaks for the deployed service.

THE CHANGE, IN FOUR PARTS.
 1. `sweep.cadence.*` reads `identity_revision_version` / `_spans` / `_merges`
    off `canonical_processed`, collected beside the `identity_revision_refusals`
    the probe already took.  The bogus item-level projection is deleted; the
    item keeps `identity_snapshot_version`, which is the version it does carry,
    with a comment naming why the other one is not there.
 2. An ABSENT field is null, never 0 or []: `versions`, `version_histogram`,
    `max_version`, `spans_revised` and `merges` go null together, with
    `spans_without_version` printed beside them.  "Measured zero revisions" and
    "measured nothing" are opposite facts about a meeting.
 3. `sweep.session_end` is filled from the post-stop `identity_finalized` drain
    or names its refusal ("identity_finalized not read: post-stop events drain
    returned 403").  That half reaches no live reader at all.
 4. Events are deduped by seq, exactly as the portal does, with the request
    unchanged; `duplicate_event_reads` and `post_stop_events.already_seen` are
    PRINTED, never subtracted silently.

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. A FIELD NAME IS AN INTERFACE, AND TWO NAMES FOR ONE IDEA IS A DEFECT ON
    BOTH SIDES.  `identity_revision_version` and `identity_snapshot_version`
    differ by one word and live one layer apart; the probe read the wrong one
    for two runs and reported a confident 0.  The fix that matters is not the
    corrected read, it is that an absent field now projects null - because the
    NEXT renamed field will be caught by the null instead of by a measurement.
 2. FIXING AN INSTRUMENT'S READ IS THE MOMENT TO AUDIT ITS OTHER READS.  The
    dedupe defect was not on any candidate list and was found only because the
    canonical-event collection was open on the screen.  It had been inflating
    `events_seen`, `event_kinds`, `spans_total` and the RTF percentiles since
    the probe was written, and `session_created: 2` was printed in every report
    the whole time.
 3. THE MIRROR CLAIM IS TESTABLE.  The probe's docstring says it mirrors the
    portal's read path; the portal dedupes by seq and the probe did not, so the
    claim was false in a way nobody had checked.  When a tool documents itself
    as a mirror, the mirrored code is a specification - read it.

BLOCKERS.  None.

/tmp/i12-f3-evidence/ralph-soak/events.tsv (the real deployed event stream),
/tmp/i9-frag-probe.json, /tmp/i9b-cont-probe.json, /tmp/i7c-probe.json.

--- context.md lines 1917-1928 - candidate 67's pre-fix description ---
    `live-pipeline-probe.py:635-637,1080` projects `item.get("identity_revision_version")` from a
    **snapshot committed item**, which carries `identity_snapshot_version` instead — a different
    quantity from a different writer (`live_session.py:165,814` vs `live_service_runtime.py:615,800`).
    The read therefore returns `None` on every span of every run, and the `isinstance(..., int)`
    filter turns that into a silent **0**. Every `live-pipeline-probe.py` report's `sweep` reduction
    is structurally blind to a cadence revision's version; it would have reported 0 on the run that
    just measured three. *Shape of the fix, not a decision:* read the version off `canonical_processed`
    (where the probe already collects `identity_revision_refusals`), and — the part that matters —
    make an **absent** field an explicit `null`/unknown rather than a 0, because this is the seventh
    instance of "a verdict word must name the thing it decides" and the third where a missing field
    was read as a negative measurement (`identity_finalized`, then `storageWrites`, now this).
    The `revised_transcript` projection beside it is correct and is what answered this iteration.

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. THE PLACES A STALE CLAIM SURVIVES ARE RANKED, AND THE RANKING IS THE OPPOSITE
    OF INTUITION.  The fifth pass found nine stale sentences in prose; this one
    found the same claim in a numbered decision and in a sequencing premise -
    i.e. in the two constructs specifically written to be trusted without
    re-derivation.  A "do not re-argue this" list is exactly where a falsified
    claim does the most damage, because its whole purpose is to stop the re-check
    that would catch it.  A pass should read the DECISIONS first, not last.
 2. A SCOREBOARD ROW AND A CANDIDATE ENTRY FOR THE SAME CLAUSE WILL DRIFT, because
    a certification run updates the one the iteration was looking at.  Both F1 and
    F3 had a stale entry under a current row.  The durable rule is now in the
    compaction log: after any certification run, correct BOTH surfaces.
 3. AN INSTRUCTION TO A FUTURE ITERATION IS NOT A CHANGE.  Iteration 12 wrote
    "re-file 65" in the body of candidate 65 and nothing re-filed it; two
    compactions read past the line.  If a rename is right, do it in the iteration
    that decides it - a deferred edit inside a block nobody re-reads is the same
    failure mode as the stale claim itself.
 4. A CROSS-REFERENCE CHECK MUST RESOLVE THE TARGET, NOT COUNT THE POINTERS.  The
    sixth pass verified the ranges it moved and reported 0 dangling references;
    a pointer broken by the FOURTH pass survived because nothing resolved it.

     (CaptureControllerTests.swift:5699, XCTAssertEqual(report.portalCycleMS,
     1_000)) compares the Swift constant TO ITSELF.  Two consequences, and the
     second is the one that matters: if the portal's cadence ever moves alone the
     gate silently mismeasures by the difference; and a PRD acceptance number can
     be improved by 500 ms by editing ONE Swift constant with NO change to what a
     human sees.  That is relaxing the gate while looking like a remedy, and
     nothing in either suite would notice.

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. A STALE CLAIM IS WORST IN THE ARTEFACT THAT LEAVES THE LOOP.  The seventh
    compaction ranked the places staleness hides - prose, then commands, then a
    "do not re-argue" decision, then a sequencing premise.  There is one rung
    above all of them: a document written FOR SOMEONE ELSE.  Working memory is
    re-read every iteration and self-corrects; an outgoing request is read once,
    by a reader who has no way to check it, and its Sec.1 is the sentence they
    act on.  Corrections must be applied to the body - a banner above a falsified
    headline leaves the headline doing the work.
 2. "NEEDS THE OPERATOR" IS NOT ONE STATE, AND CARRYING IT AS ONE COST THIS LOOP
    A PRICE IT COULD HAVE COMPUTED FIVE ITERATIONS AGO.  "F1's two REDs" sat in
    the routing rule as a single line since iteration 30 of the previous run.
    They are two different items: the RTF one genuinely needs a gate-definition
    ruling, while the latency one had a remedy NAMED IN THE PRD ITSELF and merely
    unpriced.  A batched blocker hides the members that were only one measurement
    from being actionable.  Split them in the routing rule when they are filed.
 3. THE CHEAPEST REMEDY WAS LISTED SECOND, AND ONLY CHECKING THE CONTRACT SHOWED
    IT.  The plan's ordering runs contract-expensive first.  Nothing was wrong
    with the plan - it ordered by expected effect - but "which remedy may the loop
    even touch" is a different question from "which works best", and it is
    answered by the Constraints list, not by the plan.
 4. AN ANALYTIC GATE TERM IS A CLAIM ABOUT ANOTHER PROCESS, AND IT NEEDS A TEST
    ACROSS THE BOUNDARY.  The one assertion guarding this term compares the
    constant to itself and has always passed.  This is decision 16's rule
    ("a threshold recorded out of a document is a claim about the document") one
    layer up: a constant recorded out of ANOTHER LANGUAGE'S SOURCE is a claim
    about that source, and only a cross-boundary node makes it a fact.

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. AN "HONEST LIMIT" IS A CLAIM AND IT CAN BE FALSE.  A stated limitation reads
    as epistemic humility, so nobody audits it - it is the one sentence in a
    finding that is exempt from the finding's own standard of evidence.  This one
    was wrong in its mechanism AND its arithmetic, and it sat in the outgoing
    request as the reason the operator should hesitate.  A limit deserves the
    same measurement as a result; write it with a number or write it as a
    question.
 2. "NOTHING TIES THEM" AND "THEY ARE CAUSALLY DISCONNECTED" ARE DIFFERENT
    FINDINGS, AND THE SECOND IS ACTIONABLE.  Iteration 15 proved the absence of a
    link (no test, no cross-language reference).  This iteration proved the shape
    of the two constants' effects - one moves the number and nothing else, one
    moves reality and nothing else - which is what turns "add a node" from
    hygiene into the load-bearing half of the ask.  An absence tells you nobody
    checked; a mechanism tells you what breaks.
 3. A PROBE THAT GREPS THE WORKING TREE IS NOT ASKING ABOUT THE SOURCE.  37 vs 3.
    Build output and __pycache__ answer questions about what was COMPILED, and
    every one of this loop's "nothing references X" checks is one stale artifact
    away from a false RED.  `git grep` is the surface that carries the field -
    the same rule candidate 67 paid for one layer down.
 4. THE FILE-SIZE TRIGGER MOVED UNDER THE LOOP.  The `Read` tool now PAGES
    context.md (lines 1-537 of 2293, "cap 25000 tokens", with an offset pointer)
    where the fourth compaction met a hard "exceeds maximum allowed size"
    refusal.  The compaction rationale is still sound but its stated trigger is
    stale, and a pass argued from a wall that no longer exists is a pass argued
    from the wrong reason.  Recorded in the compaction log so the eighth is
    weighed on cost-per-iteration, not on a blocked start.

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. THE PRODUCT'S FILE MODE IS WORSE THAN ITS LIVE MODE ON THE SAME AUDIO.
    -13.38 pp mean, -28.85 pp min - and the batch figure is an UPPER BOUND,
    because the probe hands Tier A a perfect local diarization, identical in both
    windows of every overlap, so its dice is 1.0 wherever a speaker is present in
    both.  A real diarizer's two windows disagree.  The gap is entirely at k>=3:
    batch scores 100% on both k=2 meetings and BEATS the album there (+7.19,
    +5.69), then falls to 63-85% from three speakers up.
 2. THE CHEAP VERSION OF STEP 4 IS RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT.  Batch Tier B moves
    duration-weighted accuracy by max |delta| = 0.0000000000 pp on every meeting,
    and it STILL does with the album's thresholds and the album's bank size
    substituted.  It is not inert - it accepted 5 links and merged real canonicals
    (19 -> 16 on k6_s1) - the merges just never touch a label the scorer counts.
    So porting ALBUM_MIN_MATCH_SCORE / _MARGIN / k into IdentityResolverConfig
    would look like unification and buy nothing.
 3. THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A THRESHOLD, AND IT IS ONE LINE.
    _tier_b_evidence:726 selects `[component for component in components if
    len(component) == 1]` - Tier B is offered ONLY singletons, so two multi-window
    chains of the same speaker can never be merged no matter what the threshold
    is.  36 of 71 components are eligible at all, and among those pairs
    cannot_link_conflict refuses 195 of 310 proposals because a singleton cannot
    link to a component that shares its window.  Step 4 must replace the linking
    structure; retuning is measured to be a no-op.
 4. BATCH FRAGMENTS THE SAME WAY LIVE DOES, FROM A DIFFERENT CAUSE.  6 speakers
    -> 19 Tier-A components -> 16-17 canonical labels, against candidate 55's 16
    on the live side.  Live fragments by birth without a duration floor; batch
    fragments by a chain Tier B may not touch.  Two defects, one symptom.
 5. TWO ENGINES, PROVED ON TRACKED SOURCE.  git grep: speaker_identity.py
    references no live identity module and live_identity{,_album,_sweep}.py
    reference no batch resolver, 0 hits each way.  The two similarity rules
    disagree by contract on the same pair - _cosine returns -1.000 unclamped where
    cosine_similarity returns 0.000 - but BOTH build a reference as a mean of
    per-interval embeddings, so at these thresholds the duplicate is a maintenance
    hazard, not a measured behavioural difference.  Decision 5's "the matcher is
    ONE function" holds on the live path and has never held across the batch seam.
 6. A CACHED-ENCODER SUBSTITUTION IS ONLY EXACT AT THE GRANULARITY THE VECTORS
    WERE EMBEDDED AT, AND THE PROBE HAD TO FAIL TWICE TO FIND THE RIGHT ONE.  The
    corpus's vector describes ALL of one (span, speaker) unit's intervals averaged
    together; _tier_b_centroid embeds one interval at a time.  Emitting one
    segment per contiguous PIECE was more faithful to a diarizer and produced 54
    cache misses (828 of 2194 units hold internal pauses); emitting one segment
    per unit's WALL EXTENT produced 1, from a unit another speaker interleaves.
    What is exact is a segment anchored at the unit's true start and given the
    unit's SPEECH seconds as its length - which also makes Tier B's 2.0 s filter
    apply to the same quantity production applies it to.  Every one of those
    misses would have been SILENTLY ABSORBED: _resolve_tier_b catches every
    encoder exception into a tier_b_embedding_failed proposal and drops that
    node's centroid, so the arm would have scored lower with no sign of why.  The
    probe asserts zero of them.

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. UNIFICATION IS WORTH +19.93 pp ON THIS CORPUS, AND THE GAIN IS ENTIRELY AT
    k>=3.  Batch already scores 100% on both two-speaker meetings; from three
    speakers up it loses 15-37 pp.  The album arm produces EXACTLY ONE CANONICAL
    PER TRUE SPEAKER - 30 births for 30 voices - against batch's 16-17 labels for
    6 speakers and candidate 55's 16 on the live side.  Both fragmentations
    disappear under the same engine.
 2. A PERFECT SCORE IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE TASK, NOT ONLY THE ENGINE, AND IT HAS TO
    BE CHECKED RATHER THAN CELEBRATED.  100.00% on every meeting was the first
    result, and reporting it as-is would have been the loop's own "known but not
    shown" defect pointed at itself.  So the probe measures the separability
    directly: a 150 s window hands the matcher 20-61 s of one speaker, where the
    WORST per-meeting gap between the lowest same-speaker cross-window cosine and
    the highest cross-speaker one is +0.190.  The task is separable.  THEREFORE
    the number to carry forward is not "batch will score 100%" but "an engine that
    loses ~20 pp on a task this separable is losing it STRUCTURALLY, NOT
    PERCEPTUALLY" - the cause and the direction, never the production number.
    That distinction is now limit 6 of the probe and 6(6) of the request.
 3. THE RULING NOW CLOSES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.  Iteration 17: batch's engine at the
    album's thresholds moves by 0.0000000000 pp.  Iteration 18: the album's engine
    at BATCH's 0.70/0.20 still wins by +19.90 pp, and ADR-0002's 0.35/0.10 is
    worth only +0.03 pp here.  And only 9 of 335 same-speaker node pairs fall
    below batch's 0.70 floor, so even that floor is not what loses the 20 pp.
    Step 4 is not a recalibration in either direction - it is the linking
    structure, as iteration 17 concluded from one side and this confirms from the
    other.
 4. TIER A ADDS ZERO ONCE THE ALBUM IS PRESENT, at its most favourable.
    album_only == tier_a_album to the digit, and the probe hands Tier A a PERFECT
    local diarization - the baseline probe's own limit, inherited.  That limit
    inflates tier_a_album and the 80.07% baseline EQUALLY and does not touch
    album_only, so the headline comparison is the conservative one.  A real
    diarizer's two windows disagree; this one's never do, and Tier A still
    contributed nothing.
 5. THE SWEEP HALF IS UNTESTED HERE AND THE PROBE SAYS SO.  Production sweep()
    proposed 0 corrections and 0 merges on the batch path, because the causal pass
    was already perfect.  That is convergence by vacuity, not evidence that step
    3's machinery helps a batch resolver - recorded as limit 8 / 6(7) rather than
    reported as a green residual.
 6. "AUTHORIZED TO WRITE" IS NOT "AUTHORIZED TO MERGE", AND THE ROUTING RULE SAID
    ONLY THE FIRST.  context.md listed step 4 under "Does NOT need an
    authorization".  Half right: prd.md authorizes the WORK, and merge-keeper.sh's
    expected_main guard refuses the NINTH merge, so the product change could be
    written and could not be landed - and would break the
    offline-probe-speaks-for-the-deployed-service invariant for every iteration
    until it was.  The routing rule is split accordingly.  This is the same shape
    the seventh compaction caught twice: a stale premise inside a decision.

WHAT THE PROBE DOES.  It degrades the local (causal) diarization pass the two
ways a real diarizer is wrong and hands the IDENTICAL labels to both engines
through ONE monkeypatched `base.build_case` - never a copy.  The batch resolver
reaches it as a bare module global, the album arm through `base.`, so the claim
"both engines saw the same input" is structural rather than asserted.  The
degradation is LABEL-ONLY (geometry, unit intervals, encoder cache and truth
untouched), a pure CRC32-seeded function of (meeting, mode, rate), and memoised,
because each arm calls build_case several times and every call must agree.

  * split   - over-segmentation: one local speaker's segments in one window cut
              into two contiguous labels.  What ADR-0002's sweep MERGE exists for.
  * confuse - label confusion: a segment attributed to another speaker present in
              the same window.  What a merge can NOT repair, so a win under split
              cannot be read as a win under any error.

THE CONTROL IS THE POINT.  `none` reproduces iteration 17's and iteration 18's
published numbers to the last digit through this harness - 80.0667 / 63.3330 /
100.0000 / 100.0000 - which is what makes the degraded rows measurements of the
ENGINES rather than of the harness.  It also reproduces both limits verbatim:
0 corrections, 0 merges (vacuous sweep) and 0 impure / 0 extra nodes (the ceiling).

  causal pass          batch    album only    album+sweep    Tier A + album
  perfect (control)    80.07    100.00        100.00         100.00
  over-segmented .30   57.84     30.50 (-27)   44.80 (-13)    79.34 (+21.50)
  over-segmented .60   42.73     17.74 (-25)   27.82 (-15)    58.58 (+15.85)
  confused .10         47.17     87.45 (+40)   87.45 (+40)    88.47 (+41.29)
  confused .25         27.06     51.06 (+24)   47.00 (+20)    47.00 (+19.94)

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. A PERFECT INPUT MAKES TWO DESIGNS INDISTINGUISHABLE, AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHEN
    A PROBE FEELS MOST CONCLUSIVE.  ADR-0002's step 4 admits two readings and
    iteration 18 measured BOTH at 100.00 %, so the choice looked free.  It is not.
    Under over-segmentation "the album replaces both tiers" is WORSE THAN THE
    ENGINE IT REPLACES (-27.34 pp, still -13.04 after the sweep) while "the album
    replaces Tier B only" wins at every condition (+21.50).  STEP 4 MUST KEEP
    TIER A, and no measurement before this one could have said so.  Iteration 18's
    finding 4 - "Tier A adds ZERO once the album is present", filed among the
    findings "recorded so they are not re-argued" - is true ONLY under the one
    condition where the arms cannot differ.  Corrected in place.
 2. THE MECHANISM IS COUNTED, NOT INFERRED, AND IT IS A UNIT-OF-ANALYSIS BUG.  At
    split@0.30 the causal pass adds 44 nodes and the album mints 6 extra
    canonicals, so 38 CUT HALVES WERE MATCHED ONTO AN EXISTING CANONICAL.
    `assign_speakers` is one-to-one WITHIN A SPAN - and A WINDOW IS NOT A SPAN.
    Two local labels in one window can be the same person, so the live path's
    one-to-one rule is FALSE on the batch path, and it pushes the second half of a
    cut turn onto ANOTHER SPEAKER - worse than a spurious birth, because it also
    poisons that speaker's centroid.  A live invariant carried onto the batch path
    unexamined is the defect, not a threshold.
 3. §6(7) IS CLOSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE USEFUL HALF.
    The sweep is NOT vacuous once the causal pass is imperfect: 25 corrections /
    6 merges worth +14.30 pp at @0.30, 23 / 16 worth +10.08 pp at @0.60, each
    reaching a FIXPOINT (residual 0).  AND IT CAN HURT: under confusion at @0.25
    the sweep moved the mean the WRONG WAY, 51.06 -> 47.00 (-4.06 pp), because a
    merge over blended centroids can join two real speakers.  Step 4's gate must
    measure both directions, not only the repair.
 4. THE CHECK I DID NOT KEEP, AND WHY THAT IS NOT WEAKENING A GATE.  The first
    draft asserted "the album beats batch under every degradation" as a FAILING
    check, and it failed twice - which is how the split result was found.  That
    assertion was my HYPOTHESIS, never a contract, and a probe whose pass
    condition is its own expected answer cannot report a surprise.  It is now a
    printed classification with the sign shown per condition, and the failing
    checks are harness integrity only: the control reproduces the published
    numbers, the degradations are non-nominal, and each sweep reaches a fixpoint.
 5. THE UNITS BUG THAT LOOKED LIKE A BROKEN CONTROL.  `lia.speaker_accuracy`
    returns a FRACTION; the first run printed "0.80 % mean" and failed all four
    control checks.  The control was exact and the reporting was wrong.  A control
    that fails is worth reading twice before the thing it controls is doubted.

THE RULE, RECORDED AS THE AMENDMENT REQUIRES.  **A birth must be enrollable.**
Evidence too short to become a REFERENCE is too short to create the speaker that
would hold one.  That is ADR-0002's matching-is-not-enrollment asymmetry applied
to the one path it never covered: the album made a fragment unable to OVERWRITE a
prototype and left it able to MINT one.  Honest about sequence: the reasoning is
in the two docstrings (`_deferred_births`, `birth_deferrals`) and was written with
the patch in one iteration, not committed ahead of it.

WHERE THE THRESHOLD LIVES, AND WHY NOT WHERE THE RULE LIVES.
`BoundedCausalIdentityPreparer` owns what a deferral MEANS; the number is the
album's own `admission_seconds`, read off the album through a new optional
provider capability `birth_deferrals(span_id, candidates)` asked for BY NAME
exactly as `take_identity_revision` and `finalize_identity` are.  Birth floor and
enrollment floor are therefore ONE NUMBER BY CONSTRUCTION - a manifest that states
`album_admission_seconds` moves both, and there is no second constant that agrees
today and drifts later.  A stack with no album defers nothing: that is
`NoLiveSpeakerEvidence`, every hand-built double, and the `policy="overwrite"`
measurement baseline, which has to keep measuring the album rather than the floor.

PER SPEAKER, NOT PER SPAN.  A deferred local publishes `UNATTRIBUTED_SPEAKER`
while a matched local in the same span keeps its label.  An abstain would drop a
label the session had every reason to write.  Two things already in the tree make
this free: `revise_labels` exempts `S00` from its collision rule (live_session.py:
616), and the coordinator already carries `local_speakers` on the PREPARED path
(live_coordinator.py:322), so a deferred unit stays addressable by a later sweep.

MEASURED - PRODUCTION OBJECTS, tests/live_identity_accuracy.py.  The control is
the capability REMOVED, which reproduces every pre-patch digit, so the deltas are
the change and not the harness.

  quantity                     before        after
  canonical speakers/meeting   16 x 8        2,2,4,3,4,4,7,6   (true k 2,2,3,3,4,4,6,6)
  live accuracy (mean)         93.44 %       99.13 %

MEASURED ON REAL CONVERSATIONAL AUDIO - the bench, 9 golden interview clips.

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. THE AMENDMENT'S FIRST CONSEQUENCE NEEDS A CORRECTION, AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC.
    "Deferred, not lost - the ledger retains it, a sweep relabels it" is true only
    ABOVE the 0.5 s evidence floor, where a vector exists to retain.  Below it
    nothing was embedded, nothing reaches the ledger, and no sweep can EVER
    relabel those words: they publish `S00` and stay `S00`.  That is the correct
    outcome - there is no evidence to identify with - but it is *not identifiable*
    rather than *deferred*, and those are different promises to a reader.  It is
    also the DOMINANT case: 14 of F2's 16 and 13 of F3's 16 canonicals came from
    exactly there.
 2. THE SECOND CONSEQUENCE CHECKED OUT, AND THE CODE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN WORDS.
    ADR-0002's "birth semantics unchanged" reads as constraining the album:
    `live_identity_album`'s docstring justifies the provisional tier BECAUSE "a
    speaker born from a 0.6 s span would have no reference at all" - the album was
    written to compensate for this defect, not to bless it.  No evidence against
    the operator's reading, so no stop-and-say-so.
 3. A LIVE CONSEQUENCE NOBODY PREDICTED: `PROVISIONAL` IS NOW UNREACHABLE.  Birth
    and admission compare the same seconds against the same threshold, so every
    born speaker is ADMITTED from its first span and the stand-in tier can never
    hold anything on the live path.  Left in place - it is the guard that keeps the
    coupling safe if a deployment ever decouples the two numbers - and filed as
    candidate 74 to be decided before Phase Q's merge.  It also strengthens the
    merge node: a merge used to be structurally unreachable (needs an admitted bank
    on both sides, and these speakers had none); it is now ELIGIBLE on every pair
    and still never fires.  "It could not" became "it could and declined".
 4. FIVE TRACKED NODES MEASURED THE DEFECT AND HAD TO BE RE-STATED, NOT DELETED.
    They are the suite's memory of candidate 55, and one of them carried a claim
    that is now FALSE: "accumulation matters more than the admission floor" -
    banked-minus-single (0.099) no longer exceeds single-minus-overwrite (0.172),
    because the birth floor lifts the WEAKEST reference policy the most (single
    exemplar 79.2 -> 89.2 against banked 93.4 -> 99.1).  A noisy reference is
    exactly what a spurious birth damages.  The flipped ordering is recorded in the
    node's own docstring as deliberately not restated.
 5. THE ONE NODE I RELAXED, AND WHY IT IS NOT WEAKENING A GATE.  The convergence
    node asserted `accuracy > live_accuracy` on EVERY meeting and a >= 4 pp mean
    gap.  Both were measuring how much the sweep had to RECOVER from a saturated
    capacity.  With the live path no longer stranding units the sweep carries
    0.5 pp and two meetings have nothing left to correct, so the per-meeting
    assertion is now "never worse" and the mean is "strictly better".  ADR-0002's
    own bar - min >= 0.97, mean >= 0.98 on the FINAL number - is untouched and
    still met at 0.9910 / 0.9965.  What moved is how much of it the reader already
    had during the meeting, which is the direction the fix was for.
 6. A SECOND HAZARD FELL OUT OF THE TEST FIXTURE, AND NO GATE SEES IT.  A manifest
    whose span cap is shorter than `album_admission_seconds` can now never birth a
    speaker and reports nothing wrong.  Found because `test_live_provider_bundle`'s
    shared `_manifest` declares `hard_cap_samples` 160 (0.01 s) against a defaulted
    1.0 s admission - two nodes flipped to `S00`.  Answered there by making that
    manifest state its own admission (0.005), which is honest for a test bundle and
    is NOT a fix for the hazard.  Deployed is safe (2.5 s cap vs 1.0 s admission).
    Filed as candidate 75; the guard belongs in `_validate_bundle`.
 7. THE BENCH IS A RE-IMPLEMENTATION, NOT THE PRODUCTION PATH, AND THAT HAD TO BE
    CHECKED BEFORE TRUSTING IT.  `proto_real_replay.py` imports the production
    EMBEDDER and mirrors live semantics with its own matcher and its own `Album`,
    so the production change does not flow through it - the birth floor had to be
    added to the bench separately (`simulate(birth_floor=)`).  Its replay also only
    ever sees units that cleared the 0.5 s evidence floor, so the never-embedded
    case cannot be represented there at all: 3.56 -> 3.00 is a LOWER BOUND.

THE DERIVATION, four independent readings over 1361 spans from FIVE real
certification directories on TWO builds (42abc5a and the deployed 7a4f59c).

  Model: elapsed = C + W(duration), so RTF = C/duration + W/duration.  The first
  term is an artifact of the denominator, not a property of the decoder.

  (1) ARITHMETIC   fastest decode ever observed 0.0564 s.  No span at or below
                   that can read RTF < 1 whatever the decoder does.
  (2) EMPIRICAL    all 15 spans shorter than 0.130 s read RTF >= 1 (1.112-5.735);
                   the shortest span that EVER read RTF < 1 is exactly 0.130 s
                   (elapsed 0.1184, RTF 0.911).  This is the reading that fixes
                   the value.
  (3) DOMINATION   Theil-Sen: elapsed = 0.0827 + 0.0890 * duration, so overhead
                   is the MAJORITY term - the amendment's own parenthetical -
                   up to 0.930 s.  The floor is 7.2x more conservative than the
                   criterion would permit.
  (4) INSENSITIVE  across 25 floors spanning 0.0564-0.930 s every one of the five
                   runs keeps the SAME verdict.

FLOOR = 0.13 s, as RTF_FLOOR_SEC in live-canary-clauses.py.  The probe IMPORTS
that constant rather than restating it, so the floor has exactly one definition
and an edit to it fails the probe instead of drifting - the same "one number by
construction" shape Q1 used for the birth floor.

WHAT THE REDUCER NOW DOES.  p95 over spans >= the floor; the excluded COUNT,
SHARE and RTF RANGE inside the verdict SENTENCE, so a verdict quoted anywhere
carries its own exclusion; the unfiltered p95 still printed above it "for the
record"; a span from an older event schema with no frozen_span_duration_sec
COUNTED, never excluded; and a NEW aggregate-RTF clause gated beside the p95 -
total decode seconds over total audio seconds across EVERY span, nothing
excluded.  UNDECIDED (never green) when every span is below the floor, or when
fewer than RTF_MIN_GATED_SPANS = 20 are above it.

WHAT I LEARNED.
 1. THE ONE ARBITRARY NUMBER I WROTE WAS THE ONE THAT BROKE, AND IT BROKE AS
    CANDIDATE 57's DEFECT.  A 5% exclusion-share cap went in first "to stop the
    floor doing too much work"; it promptly called F1 it.30 UNDECIDED at 3
    excluded spans of 52 - a run with 49 gated spans that plainly CAN answer the
    clause.  That is "a verdict word must name the thing it decides", re-broken
    four candidates after it was paid for.  It is also not the hazard: a meeting
    with many brief utterances is a legitimate meeting, and every excluded span's
    decode cost is still charged in full to the aggregate.  Replaced by a
    SAMPLE-SIZE guard derived from the estimator - below n=20 a nearest-rank p95
    IS the maximum wearing a percentile's name - which moves no run in the corpus
    (smallest gated population 46).  I removed it because it was wrong, not
    because it failed; the distinction is the whole of the discipline here.
 2. "CONSERVATIVE" IS AMBIGUOUS AND COST A REWRITE OF MY OWN REASONING.  I first
    wrote "take the smallest end of the insensitivity plateau", which implies
    0.057 - and that is NOT more careful, it is an UNDER-application: it leaves in
    the 0.111 s and 0.120 s spans that also never discriminated.  Conservatism's
    real work here was choosing the EMPIRICAL boundary (0.13) over the DOMINATION
    point the amendment's own parenthetical would have allowed (0.93, 7.2x more
    exclusions).  Both files now say which reading governs.
 3. THE HONEST GUARD AGAINST LAUNDERING IS NOT A CAP ON THE EXCLUSION, IT IS A
    STATISTIC THE EXCLUSION CANNOT REACH.  Aggregate RTF over every span makes the
    floor unable to hide a backlog no matter how large it is, which is why the
    share cap was redundant as well as wrong.
 4. THE FLOOR MUST NOT SELF-CALIBRATE, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO.  The same
    robust fit applied to each run ALONE puts C/m between 0.590 s and 2.007 s: a
    60 s canary has ~50 spans and the fit follows whichever runaway decodes it
    happened to see.  A per-run floor would move with exactly the noise it exists
    to be immune to.  Recorded in the probe's docstring so it is not re-proposed.
 5. TWO REAL BUGS IN MY OWN FIRST CUT, both found only by driving the flag.  The
    classification read the MODULE CONSTANT instead of args.rtf_floor_sec, so
    `--rtf-floor-sec` moved nothing and both UNDECIDED paths were unreachable -
    the flag looked like it worked because the default equals the constant.  And
    the probe CRASHED at floor 0 (empty `below`, then a divide-by-zero) instead
    of failing cleanly: a probe that raises where it should report FAIL is a probe
    that cannot be used to red-prove anything.
 6. F1's TWO REDs WERE NEVER ONE PROBLEM.  The RTF red was an instrument defect
    and is now answered without touching the service; the 4150.8 ms latency red is
    real, priced at iteration 15, and needs the operator.  The scoreboard row said
    "TWO RED" and both the row and candidate 70 now say so - the corollary the
    seventh compaction paid for twice.
 7. A CHECK THAT HAS NEVER FAILED IS NOT NECESSARILY A CHECK THAT PASSES.  The
    compaction log's own verification recipe says the surviving Validation fence
    must pass `bash -n`.  Run as written it FAILS at HEAD, and has since at least
    the M6c entry - not because a command is malformed but because bash parses
    PROSE: a backtick inside a comment opens a command substitution once an
    earlier odd apostrophe has closed the quote that was hiding it, so
    `simulate(birth_floor=)` and `rollback: mv <backup> <output>` both abort the
    parse.  The check that means what the fence promises is commands-only -
    `... | grep -v '^#' | bash -n` - which is rc=0 over 93 command lines at HEAD
    and after this iteration.  The recipe in the compaction log is corrected in
    place.  I did NOT edit iteration 21's prose to satisfy the broken check: the
    check was wrong, not the prose.
